weapons.name: Wanderer's Arming Sword
weapons.description: Issued to anyone who swore to walk the roads and report what they found. Nobody has filed a report in a long while. The grip is wrapped in three different hands' worth of cloth.

weapons.name: Vigilkeeper's Longsword
weapons.description: The Vigil counted the hours aloud so the dead would know time still passed. The blade is notched every hundred nights; the notches stop, then start again in a different hand.

weapons.name: Pale Choir Broadsword
weapons.description: Cast from the metal of a bell that cracked mid-hymn. It still wants to finish the note, and hums when swung, and hums a little afterwards.

weapons.name: Oath of the Empty Chair
weapons.description: The Hollow King's own blade, sworn to a throne he would not sit in. He said a crown was only a promise you could take off. Then he did not take it off, and could not, and stopped trying.

weapons.name: Roadwarden's Greatsword
weapons.description: Too heavy for a road and too dull for a war. Roadwardens carried them anyway, because a thing this size ends an argument before it begins.

weapons.name: Frostmarch Greatsword
weapons.description: Left in the open one winter to see whether the cold would ruin it. The cold moved in instead, and pays no rent, and will not be asked to leave.

weapons.name: Ashen Warden's Cleaver
weapons.description: The Warden kept the road for two hundred years after the road forgot where it went. There is no edge left on this. It has not needed one in some time.

weapons.name: Gravehauler
weapons.description: Not a sword. A door-bar from a crypt, sharpened by a man who had been inside it. He walked out. The door did not.

weapons.name: Pillar of the Pale Choir
weapons.description: A load-bearing column of a hall that no longer needs bearing. Whatever it held up is still up there, somehow, over nothing.

weapons.name: Cinderward, the Kept Flame
weapons.description: The First Flame Knight was told to keep the fire. He was not told for how long, or for whom, and no one came back to say stop. The steel has been red for so long it has forgotten grey.

weapons.name: Hollowwood Katana
weapons.description: Folded from nails pulled out of the Hollowwood shrines when the shrines stopped answering. It cuts cleanly and resents being thanked.

weapons.name: Mourner's Edge
weapons.description: Carried at funerals, point down, so the dead could see it was not for them. Eventually it was always for them.

weapons.name: Frost Tongue
weapons.description: Quenched in meltwater from a glacier that had a village under it. The village is still there. The glacier has moved on.

weapons.name: Brigand's Falchion
weapons.description: Made from a scythe by a man who decided the harvest was over. He was right, in the end, though not in the way he meant.

weapons.name: Saltwind Falchion
weapons.description: The Palewaste eats iron in a season. This one is on its ninth season and has stopped losing weight, which nobody can explain.

weapons.name: Duelist's Needle
weapons.description: Duels were how the old court settled inheritance. When the court hollowed, the duels continued out of habit, and the inheritances got smaller.

weapons.name: Court Estoc
weapons.description: Long enough to reach a man across a dinner table. That was, at one point, the fashion, and then for a while it was the necessity.

weapons.name: Graverobber's Knife
weapons.description: Short, because the graves are shallow. Curved, because the dead here hold on.

weapons.name: Ashen Stiletto
weapons.description: Thin enough to slip between the plates of a knight who has stopped maintaining his armour. Most of them have.

weapons.name: Rot-Kissed Fang
weapons.description: Left in the Mirefen a year on a dare. The dare was won. Nobody wanted to touch the winnings, so they left it there another year, and it improved.

weapons.name: Roadman's Pike
weapons.description: The cheapest way to keep something at arm's length, and arm's length is the whole of the old law.

weapons.name: Sunken March Spear
weapons.description: Fisher's tool, then soldier's tool, then fisher's tool again. The March keeps changing what it needs and never asks.

weapons.name: Vesselbind, the Last Lit Thing
weapons.description: A shard of the Bright Spirit, held in a shaft of ordinary ash wood by ordinary twine. That is all it ever was: something bright, and something willing to carry it.

weapons.name: Watchtower Halberd
weapons.description: Built to push a ladder off a wall. The walls fell without help. The habit remains.

weapons.name: Mirefen Guisarme
weapons.description: The hook is for pulling things out of the water. Some of what comes out is not what went in.

weapons.name: Bell-Ringer's Glaive
weapons.description: The ringers were also the guards; nobody could afford two sets of men. Strike a bell hard enough and it is a weapon. Strike a man hard enough and he is a bell.

weapons.name: Woodcutter's Great Axe
weapons.description: The Hollowwood does not grow and does not rot, so the woodcutters had nothing to cut. They kept the axes. Something always turns up.

weapons.name: Cinder Flats Cleaver
weapons.description: Heated once, deliberately, past the point of usefulness, by a smith who wanted to know what steel would do if you asked too much of it. It does this.

weapons.name: Headsman's Burden
weapons.description: Executions in the Palewaste were performed kneeling and were considered a mercy, since the alternative was to be let go.

weapons.name: Hearth Axe
weapons.description: Kindling, mostly. It has done other things, once or twice, and does not distinguish.

weapons.name: Boneknapper Axe
weapons.description: Head chipped from the femur of something the Bone Orchard grew. It holds an edge better than iron and screams in the cold, quietly, at a pitch you feel rather than hear.

weapons.name: Pilgrim's Mace
weapons.description: Clergy were forbidden to draw blood. This draws none, which was the letter of it, and everyone was satisfied with the letter.

weapons.name: Reliquary Mace
weapons.description: The head is a small locked box. Something rattles inside. It has not been opened, on the grounds that it works.

weapons.name: Censer of the Late Hour
weapons.description: Swung on a chain at the last service of the day, to send the smoke up where the light used to be. The service ran late. It is still running.

weapons.name: Stonemason's Maul
weapons.description: The masons went from building to unbuilding without changing tools, which they said proved something about masonry.

weapons.name: Avalanche Maul
weapons.description: Named for what it starts, not for what it is. The mountain does most of the work; you only have to ask it once, loudly.

weapons.name: Anchor of the Long Winter
weapons.description: The Colossus carried this to hold the season in place, the way a stone holds a page. Winter has not moved since. It is not clear whether that was the intention or the accident.

weapons.name: Knotted Club
weapons.description: A branch that grew around a stone and would not give it back. Somebody put a strap on it and called it a weapon, and it agreed.

weapons.name: Rootwood Greatclub
weapons.description: Rootwood does not burn and does not float and will not take a nail. There is nothing to do with it but hit.

weapons.name: Tanner's Whip
weapons.description: For driving beasts that had stopped listening. Later, for driving off things that had never listened at all.

weapons.name: Thorn of the Long Road
weapons.description: Braided with the black brier that grows only where a road has been abandoned. Nine strands. Nine roads.

weapons.name: Paired Pilgrim Blades
weapons.description: Two pilgrims set out. One came back with both halves and would not explain the join.

weapons.name: Rift-Split Twinblade
weapons.description: It was one blade. The Rift disagreed. Now it is two, joined at the disagreement.

weapons.name: Paired Silence
weapons.description: The Seraph had two hands and nothing at all to say with either. Struck together, these make no sound whatsoever, and the absence carries further than noise.

weapons.name: Harvest Scythe
weapons.description: The last harvest was brought in on time by people who already knew there would be no next one. They were very thorough.

weapons.name: Blightborn Reaper
weapons.description: Grown, not forged. The Mirefen makes tools sometimes, the way a wound makes a scar, and with the same intention.

weapons.name: Tithe of the Slow Tide
weapons.description: The Mirelord took one in ten of everything the fen swallowed, and gave back nine, changed. This is what he counted with.

weapons.name: Crawler's Claws
weapons.description: Harvested, fitted to a leather cuff, worn by people who decided the crawlers had the right idea about hands.

weapons.name: Revenant Talons
weapons.description: Taken off a revenant that had grown them without ever having had hands to grow them from. It wanted something badly enough to build the tools for it.

weapons.name: Pilgrim's Knuckles
weapons.description: Iron rings worn on the road, one added at each shrine. The devout arrive with heavy hands.

weapons.name: Emberfist Gauntlets
weapons.description: A coal is placed in each palm before a fight and is expected to still be warm afterwards. It always is. Nobody has asked what feeds it.

weapons.name: Hunter's Shortbow
weapons.description: The game left before the people did. The bows outlasted both, being cheap and useful and hard to eat.

weapons.name: Hollowwood Longbow
weapons.description: Cut from a tree that was already dead and had not noticed. It draws smoothly and never warps, and does not care for the weather at all.

weapons.name: Bone Orchard Bow
weapons.description: Limbs of rib, string of tendon, nocks of tooth. Everything in the Orchard is made of the Orchard; that is the whole of the horticulture.

weapons.name: Siege Greatbow
weapons.description: Braced against the ground and fired at whatever was slow enough to still be there. Almost everything is, now.

weapons.name: Wallbreaker Greatbow
weapons.description: It never broke a wall. It broke the men standing behind one, through it, which was judged close enough to keep the name.

weapons.name: Light Crossbow
weapons.description: Requires no skill, no strength and no courage, and was therefore the most common weapon in the kingdom by a very wide margin.

weapons.name: Winch Crossbow
weapons.description: Forty turns of the crank per shot. Forty turns is a long time to look at what you are about to do.

weapons.name: Gravebolt Repeater
weapons.description: Built by a smith who had six shots' worth of enemies and one shot's worth of courage. The arithmetic held.

weapons.name: Apprentice Spirit Staff
weapons.description: The first lesson is that the light is not yours. The second lesson is how to hold it anyway. There is no third lesson; the school is gone.

weapons.name: Choir Staff
weapons.description: Tuned rather than forged. Held wrong, it drones. Held right, it does not make a sound and something else does.

weapons.name: Voice of the Seventh Bell
weapons.description: Six bells were rung for the dead and one for the living. The seventh has not been rung since there was any reason to. It remembers the shape of the note.

weapons.name: Pilgrim's Seal
weapons.description: Pressed into wax to certify a prayer was said. Pressed into a palm, it certifies rather more.

weapons.name: Pyre-Tender's Seal
weapons.description: The tenders fed the pyres so the dead would not walk. The dead walk. The tenders feed the pyres. Neither party has agreed to stop first.

weapons.name: The Eighteenth Knot
weapons.description: The Shepherd kept his count on a cord, a knot for each stone in the ring. There are eighteen knots. There have been seventeen stones since before anyone now living was told the number. He would not untie it and he would not stop short, so he begins again, and the last knot closes on nothing, and he counts it anyway.

weapons.name: The Held Heat
weapons.description: He was ordered to keep the forge lit until relieved, and he kept everything in it — the fire, the work, the light, himself. These are what he kept it with. They have not been opened since the March went under, and they are far too warm to be closed on nothing.

weapons.name: Ribwood, What the Pit Grew
weapons.description: Nobody cut this and nobody strung it. It came up out of the Long Pit already curved, already taut, in the shape of something that had been given a great deal for a very long time and had begun to have views about what it was for.

weapons.name: The Lamp That Was Not Lit
weapons.description: Somebody carried this the whole length of the Hollow of Lights and never once struck it, on the theory that a lamp you have not lit cannot go out. They were right, and it did not help them, and it is still full.

weapons.name: Every Road at Once
weapons.description: A lance that will not agree to one line. Point it and it takes all the ways it might have gone, which is a great deal more convenient for you than it is for the country in front of you.

weapons.name: Ninefold, and Counting
weapons.description: The ninth cut was the one that worked and the cutter did not stop there. Nobody has established what the current number is; the rod declines to be measured and the cold coming off it is answer enough.

weapons.name: Answerer
weapons.description: Ordinary in the hand and ordinary in the scabbard. What it does is arrive at the second man and the third while the first is still deciding whether he was struck, and it has never been persuaded to stop at one.

weapons.name: The Tithe Collected
weapons.description: The fen takes one in ten. This takes the ten and hands you back the one, which is not generosity, only bookkeeping performed in your favour for reasons it has not disclosed.

weapons.name: The Long Winter, Held
weapons.description: They pinned the season to the Frostmarch and somebody had to hold the pin. This is the pin. It is heavier than a season has any business being and it has not been put down.

weapons.name: Red Arithmetic
weapons.description: The Orchard was planted deliberately and harvested the same way, and somewhere in the middle of that somebody worked out that a wound in one body is a proposition about every body nearby. This is the proof.

weapons.name: Hearth, Carried
weapons.description: Every fire in the kingdom was lit from the Flats and this was how the Flats travelled. It does not go out between swings. It does not go out between owners.

weapons.name: The Sixth Hall Answers
weapons.description: Six halls singing and a seventh listening. Hold this and the sixth hall answers you personally, in a voice that costs it nothing and gives you back rather more than you spent.

weapons.name: Open Question
weapons.description: Four cuts that do not close. The Orchard grew these on something and then took them off it, and the something is generally agreed to have been asking for it.

weapons.name: Second Sun
weapons.description: The tenders argue about almost everything and are unanimous about this: it should not have been made, it cannot be unmade, and whoever is holding it should be somewhere else.

weapons.name: The Still Hour
weapons.description: Nine cairns and between the eighth and the ninth there is an hour where nothing moves and the snow hangs. Somebody brought a needle into that hour and came out with this.

weapons.name: Two Lanterns, One Wick
weapons.description: Court work from the last years, when the court had stopped pretending. Two blades, one light between them, and it keeps burning in the carrier as long as the carrier keeps carrying.

weapons.name: What the Ground Owes
weapons.description: Driven into the Mirefen as a marker and pulled out again nine years later by somebody who needed a spear more than they needed a marker. It has been collecting the whole time and it settles up through you.

weapons.name: Bog-Iron Arming Sword of the Hollowwood Verge
weapons.description: Bog-iron takes a poor edge and holds a long grudge. Short in the blade and quick back to guard.

weapons.name: Grey Steel Cleaver-Sword of the Vigilkeepers
weapons.description: Grey steel: the kingdom’s standard, back when there were standards. Weighted forward like a butcher’s tool, because it began as one.

weapons.name: Bone Orchard Kept Iron Broadsword
weapons.description: Kept iron is oiled, wrapped and re-wrapped by people with nothing else to keep. It was hung in the Bone Orchard for years before anyone took it down.

weapons.name: Salt-Iron Fenwright Longsword
weapons.description: Fenwright work: they keep nine parts and give the tenth to the water. The measured, unfashionable length that ends most arguments.

weapons.name: Cinder Flats Estoc-Blade in Bonesteel
weapons.description: Sworn to the First Hearth, whatever that was worth by the end. Bonesteel is folded with ash of the dead, which the smiths insist is only for carbon.

weapons.name: Tomb-Lead Arming Sword of the Hollow Court
weapons.description: Tomb-lead was cast to seal something in. It is heavy in a way that feels deliberate. It was hung in the Hollow Court for years before anyone took it down.

weapons.name: Rift-Scar Cleaver-Sword in Quicksilvered Steel
weapons.description: Taken out of the wound the light left going out. Quicksilvered, so the edge stays bright and the hand stays cold.

weapons.name: Cinder-Bronze Roadwarden’s Broadsword
weapons.description: Broad enough that the flat of it is a tool in its own right. Someone in the Roadwardens thought cinder-bronze would improve on that.

weapons.name: Mirefen Hoarfrost Steel Longsword
weapons.description: Recovered from the Mirefen, still serviceable. Hoarfrost steel sweats in warm rooms and rings a half-tone flat.

weapons.name: Choir-Marble Estoc-Blade of the Turned Earth
weapons.description: Narrowed almost to a spike, meant for the gaps in things. Kept in the Gravewards against a day that came, and went, without it.

weapons.name: Meteor-Glass Arming Sword of the Sixth Hall
weapons.description: Meteor-glass fell already shaped, which nobody enjoys thinking about. Seven halls, six of them singing, and this was made in one of the six. Short in the blade and quick back to guard.

weapons.name: Pyre-Tender’s Riftglass Cleaver-Sword
weapons.description: Riftglass is the Scar’s own leavings, and it is never quite where you last put it. Weighted forward like a butcher’s tool, because it began as one.

weapons.name: Bog-Iron Estoc-Blade of the Long Winter
weapons.description: Narrowed almost to a spike, meant for the gaps in things. Bog-iron takes a poor edge and holds a long grudge. The rest is guesswork.

weapons.name: Grey Steel Arming Sword of the Hollow of Lights
weapons.description: Made in the Hollow of Lights, of grey steel. Short in the blade and quick back to guard.

weapons.name: Grey Strand Cleaver-Sword in Salt-Iron
weapons.description: Salt-iron is pitted all over and somehow sharper for it. Everything that floated came to the Strand and stopped, and this came with it. It still balances.

weapons.name: Bonesteel Ashen Reach Broadsword
weapons.description: Bonesteel is folded with ash of the dead, which the smiths insist is only for carbon. Made on the Reach, where the ground is grey and level and much deeper than it looks. It still balances.

weapons.name: Tomb-Lead Longsword of the Sunken March
weapons.description: A tomb-lead longsword, out of the Sunken March. The measured, unfashionable length that ends most arguments.

weapons.name: Quicksilvered Steel Estoc-Blade of the Held Note
weapons.description: Narrowed almost to a spike, meant for the gaps in things. Quicksilvered, so the edge stays bright and the hand stays cold. The rest is guesswork.

weapons.name: Palewaste Pale Ivory Arming Sword
weapons.description: Salt where a capital was, and this was dug out of the salt. Pale ivory, carved thin enough to see the lamp through. You can feel where the last owner held it.

weapons.name: Cairnward Cleaver-Sword in Cinder-Bronze
weapons.description: Recovered from the Cairnwards, still serviceable. Cinder-bronze holds warmth for hours after it should have gone cold.

weapons.name: Choir-Marble Broadsword of the Long Road
weapons.description: Broad enough that the flat of it is a tool in its own right. Someone in the Hollowwood Verge thought choir-marble would improve on that.

weapons.name: Meteor-Glass Longsword of the Vigilkeepers
weapons.description: A vigilkeeper’s issue, stamped on the tang and never once relieved. Meteor-glass fell already shaped, which nobody enjoys thinking about.

weapons.name: Riftglass Estoc-Blade of the Planted Dead
weapons.description: The Orchard was planted deliberately, and this was harvested from it the same way. It has been re-wrapped twice and re-ground more often than that.

weapons.name: Bog-Iron Broadsword of the Ninth Part
weapons.description: Broad enough that the flat of it is a tool in its own right. Kept in the Fenwrights against a day that came, and went, without it.

weapons.name: Cinder Flats Longsword in Grey Steel
weapons.description: The measured, unfashionable length that ends most arguments. Every fire in the kingdom was lit from the Flats, including the one that made this. There is a name scratched under the grip, worn past reading.

weapons.name: Hollow Court Estoc-Blade in Kept Iron
weapons.description: Court work from the last years, when the court had stopped pretending. The kept iron is the only part that has not been replaced.

weapons.name: Salt-Iron Arming Sword of the Wound
weapons.description: Short in the blade and quick back to guard. Taken out of the wound the light left going out. There is a name scratched under the grip, worn past reading.

weapons.name: Roadwarden’s Cleaver-Sword in Tomb-Lead
weapons.description: Tomb-lead was cast to seal something in. It is heavy in a way that feels deliberate. Issued to a warden who was told to walk the road and report what they found. Weighted forward like a butcher’s tool, because it began as one.

weapons.name: Quicksilvered Steel Broadsword of the Tithe
weapons.description: Quicksilvered, so the edge stays bright and the hand stays cold. Broad enough that the flat of it is a tool in its own right. Nobody in the Mirefen signed it.

weapons.name: Pale Ivory Graveward Longsword
weapons.description: The longsword pattern, as the Gravewards understood it. Pale ivory, carved thin enough to see the lamp through.

weapons.name: Cinder-Bronze Estoc-Blade of the Sixth Hall
weapons.description: Cinder-bronze holds warmth for hours after it should have gone cold. Narrowed almost to a spike, meant for the gaps in things.

weapons.name: Hoarfrost Steel Arming Sword of the Kept Flame
weapons.description: Made in the Pyre-Tenders, of hoarfrost steel. Short in the blade and quick back to guard.

weapons.name: Choir-Marble Cleaver-Sword of the Frostmarch
weapons.description: Weighted forward like a butcher’s tool, because it began as one. The season was pinned to the Frostmarch and never released; the steel remembers.

weapons.name: Hollowlight Broadsword in Meteor-Glass
weapons.description: Broad enough that the flat of it is a tool in its own right. Meteor-glass fell already shaped, which nobody enjoys thinking about. From where it fell, and where, if you stand still long enough, it is still falling.

weapons.name: Grey Strand Bog-Iron Arming Sword
weapons.description: Short in the blade and quick back to guard. Kept in the Grey Strand against a day that came, and went, without it.

weapons.name: Grey Steel Cleaver-Sword of the Level Ground
weapons.description: Made on the Reach, where the ground is grey and level and much deeper than it looks. The grey steel is the only part that has not been replaced.

weapons.name: Kept Iron Sunken March Broadsword
weapons.description: Broad enough that the flat of it is a tool in its own right. Kept iron is oiled, wrapped and re-wrapped by people with nothing else to keep. The rest is guesswork.

weapons.name: Salt-Iron Longsword of the Held Note
weapons.description: The measured, unfashionable length that ends most arguments. Salt-iron is pitted all over and somehow sharper for it. The rest is guesswork.

weapons.name: Bonesteel Estoc-Blade of the Empty Chair
weapons.description: Narrowed almost to a spike, meant for the gaps in things. Bonesteel is folded with ash of the dead, which the smiths insist is only for carbon. Salt where a capital was, and this was dug out of the salt.

weapons.name: Tomb-Lead Cairnward Arming Sword
weapons.description: Tomb-lead was cast to seal something in. It is heavy in a way that feels deliberate. Short in the blade and quick back to guard. Nobody in the Cairnwards signed it.

weapons.name: Hollowwood Bastard Blade in Bog-Iron
weapons.description: They made these in the Hollowwood Verge by the dozen, and this is the one that came back. Sized for one hand by someone who never uses one hand.

weapons.name: Roadwarden’s War Greatsword in Quicksilvered Steel
weapons.description: Quicksilvered, so the edge stays bright and the hand stays cold. Plain, long, and built to be swung all day. Nobody in the Roadwardens signed it.

weapons.name: Grey Strand Bastard Blade in Riftglass
weapons.description: Riftglass is the Scar’s own leavings, and it is never quite where you last put it. Sized for one hand by someone who never uses one hand.

weapons.name: Tomb-Lead Vigilkeep Tombblade
weapons.description: A tombblade in tomb-lead, in the Vigilkeep manner. A vigilkeeper’s issue, stamped on the tang and never once relieved.

weapons.name: Meteor-Glass Waved Greatsword of the Mirefen
weapons.description: The fen takes one in ten of everything and gives back things like this. It has been re-wrapped twice and re-ground more often than that.

weapons.name: Bonesteel Bastard Blade of the Ashen Reach
weapons.description: Made on the Reach, where the ground is grey and level and much deeper than it looks. Bonesteel is folded with ash of the dead, which the smiths insist is only for carbon. You can feel where the last owner held it.

weapons.name: Choir-Marble War Greatsword of the Planted Dead
weapons.description: Choir-marble is quarried from the halls themselves, which the Choir permits and does not forgive. Made for the Planted Dead, and outlived it comfortably.

weapons.name: Graveward Salt-Iron Waved Greatsword
weapons.description: A salt-iron waved greatsword, out of the Gravewards. The edge runs in slow waves, so every cut drags.

weapons.name: Hoarfrost Steel Sunken March Tombblade
weapons.description: Heavy at the tip, the way grave-slabs are heavy at the far end. Out of the province that agreed to go under and never came back up.

weapons.name: Kept Iron War Greatsword of the Ninth Part
weapons.description: Kept iron is oiled, wrapped and re-wrapped by people with nothing else to keep. Plain, long, and built to be swung all day.

weapons.name: Cinder-Bronze Bastard Blade of the Sixth Hall
weapons.description: Sized for one hand by someone who never uses one hand. Cinder-bronze holds warmth for hours after it should have gone cold. The rest is guesswork.

weapons.name: Grey Steel Tombblade of the Bell-Ringers
weapons.description: Recovered from the Bell-Ringers, still serviceable. Grey steel: the kingdom’s standard, back when there were standards.

weapons.name: Cinder Flats Pale Ivory Waved Greatsword
weapons.description: Every fire in the kingdom was lit from the Flats, including the one that made this. Pale ivory, carved thin enough to see the lamp through. You can feel where the last owner held it.

weapons.name: Bog-Iron Pyre-Tender’s Bastard Blade
weapons.description: Bog-iron takes a poor edge and holds a long grudge. Tender’s work, from an order that argues constantly and never lets the fire go out. Sized for one hand by someone who never uses one hand.

weapons.name: Palewaste Quicksilvered Steel War Greatsword
weapons.description: Salt where a capital was, and this was dug out of the salt. Plain, long, and built to be swung all day.

weapons.name: Riftglass Bastard Blade of the Abdication
weapons.description: Sized for one hand by someone who never uses one hand. Kept in the Hollow Court against a day that came, and went, without it.

weapons.name: Frostmarch Tombblade in Tomb-Lead
weapons.description: The season was pinned to the Frostmarch and never released; the steel remembers. Tomb-lead was cast to seal something in. It is heavy in a way that feels deliberate. You can feel where the last owner held it.

weapons.name: Cairnward Waved Greatsword in Meteor-Glass
weapons.description: Meteor-glass fell already shaped, which nobody enjoys thinking about. The edge runs in slow waves, so every cut drags. Nobody in the Cairnwards signed it.

weapons.name: Bonesteel Bastard Blade of the Rift Scar
weapons.description: Sized for one hand by someone who never uses one hand. Taken out of the wound the light left going out. There is a name scratched under the grip, worn past reading.

weapons.name: Choir-Marble War Greatsword of the Falling Light
weapons.description: A choir-marble war greatsword, out of the Hollow of Lights. Plain, long, and built to be swung all day.

weapons.name: Bonesteel Waved Greatsword of the Hollowwood Verge
weapons.description: Recovered from the Hollowwood Verge, still serviceable. Bonesteel is folded with ash of the dead, which the smiths insist is only for carbon.

weapons.name: Choir-Marble Tombblade of the Road Law
weapons.description: Issued to a warden who was told to walk the road and report what they found. Heavy at the tip, the way grave-slabs are heavy at the far end.

weapons.name: Grey Strand Salt-Iron War Greatsword
weapons.description: Sworn to the Slow Salt, whatever that was worth by the end. Salt-iron is pitted all over and somehow sharper for it.

weapons.name: Hoarfrost Steel Bastard Blade of the Vigilkeepers
weapons.description: A vigilkeeper’s issue, stamped on the tang and never once relieved. Hoarfrost steel sweats in warm rooms and rings a half-tone flat. You can feel where the last owner held it.

weapons.name: Mirefen Tombblade in Kept Iron
weapons.description: Kept iron is oiled, wrapped and re-wrapped by people with nothing else to keep. Made for the Tithe, and outlived it comfortably.

weapons.description: A blightprism grew in the water rather than being cut, and the light that leaves it has been somewhere. Short, quick, and honest about how little it aims. Nobody in the Roadwardens signed it.

weapons.name: Blightprism Palewaste Cut-Prism Rod
weapons.description: A blightprism grew in the water rather than being cut, and the light that leaves it has been somewhere. One clean cut through the stone, and everything after it is arithmetic.

weapons.name: Graveward Long Prism in Chorded Brass
weapons.description: A graveward’s tool, and they were not fussy about which of its uses came first. A hand and a half of ground glass. It reaches further than it has any right to.

weapons.name: Hollowwood Red Prism Splitter Rod
weapons.description: A red prism splitter rod, out of the Hollowwood Verge. The bolt leaves as three and arrives as one, mostly.

weapons.name: Red Prism Hand Prism of the Pyre-Tenders
weapons.description: Palmed. Nobody sees it until the room changes colour. Tender’s work, from an order that argues constantly and never lets the fire go out.

weapons.name: Bone Orchard Scatter Wand in Drawn Arcwire
weapons.description: Recovered from the Bone Orchard, still serviceable. Drawn a hair at a time, over years, by people who could not be told why it had to be one piece.

weapons.name: Drawn Arcwire Cut-Prism Rod of the Hollow of Lights
weapons.description: From where it fell, and where, if you stand still long enough, it is still falling. It has been re-wrapped twice and re-ground more often than that.

weapons.name: Cinder Flats Voidglass Long Prism
weapons.description: A hand and a half of ground glass. It reaches further than it has any right to. Every fire in the kingdom was lit from the Flats, including the one that made this. There is a name scratched under the grip, worn past reading.

weapons.name: Ashen Reach Stormglass Scatter Wand
weapons.description: Short, quick, and honest about how little it aims. Someone in the Ashen Reach thought stormglass would improve on that.

weapons.name: Stormglass Cut-Prism Rod of the Rift Scar
weapons.description: Stormglass is fulgurite, dug up whole where the sky touched down and went away again. One clean cut through the stone, and everything after it is arithmetic. Nobody in the Rift Scar signed it.

weapons.name: Hoarlens Long Prism of the Held Note
weapons.description: A hand and a half of ground glass. It reaches further than it has any right to. A ringer’s piece, balanced for someone whose arms already knew the rhythm.

weapons.name: Emberlens Splitter Rod of the Tithe
weapons.description: An emberlens is fire-glass, and you can see the moment it was made trapped inside it. The bolt leaves as three and arrives as one, mostly. Nobody in the Mirefen signed it.

weapons.name: Cairnward Hand Prism in Emberlens
weapons.description: An emberlens is fire-glass, and you can see the moment it was made trapped inside it. Made for the Nine Cairns, and outlived it comfortably.

weapons.name: Blightprism Scatter Wand of the Sixth Hall
weapons.description: Seven halls, six of them singing, and this was made in one of the six. Short, quick, and honest about how little it aims.

weapons.name: Chorded Brass Cut-Prism Rod of the Kept Watch
weapons.description: A vigilkeeper’s issue, stamped on the tang and never once relieved. It has been re-wrapped twice and re-ground more often than that.

weapons.name: Frostmarch Long Prism in Chorded Brass
weapons.description: A hand and a half of ground glass. It reaches further than it has any right to. The season was pinned to the Frostmarch and never released; the steel remembers. There is a name scratched under the grip, worn past reading.

weapons.name: Fenwright Red Prism Splitter Rod
weapons.description: A red prism splitter rod, out of the Fenwrights. The bolt leaves as three and arrives as one, mostly.

weapons.name: Drawn Arcwire Hand Prism of the Slow Salt
weapons.description: Drawn a hair at a time, over years, by people who could not be told why it had to be one piece. Palmed. Nobody sees it until the room changes colour.

weapons.name: Drawn Arcwire Scatter Wand of the Hollow Court
weapons.description: Drawn a hair at a time, over years, by people who could not be told why it had to be one piece. Short, quick, and honest about how little it aims. Nobody in the Hollow Court signed it.

weapons.name: Sunken March Cut-Prism Rod in Voidglass
weapons.description: Voidglass is what the Hollow of Lights leaves behind, and it is colder on the side away from you. One clean cut through the stone, and everything after it is arithmetic. Nobody in the Sunken March signed it.

weapons.name: Roadwarden’s Hand Prism in Stormglass
weapons.description: Palmed. Nobody sees it until the room changes colour. Stormglass is fulgurite, dug up whole where the sky touched down and went away again. The rest is guesswork.

weapons.name: Palewaste Stormglass Scatter Wand
weapons.description: Short, quick, and honest about how little it aims. Stormglass is fulgurite, dug up whole where the sky touched down and went away again. The rest is guesswork.

weapons.name: Hoarlens Graveward Cut-Prism Rod
weapons.description: A graveward’s tool, and they were not fussy about which of its uses came first. The hoarlens is the only part that has not been replaced.

weapons.name: Stormglass Coil Lance of the Hollowwood Verge
weapons.description: Sworn to the Long Road, whatever that was worth by the end. Stormglass is fulgurite, dug up whole where the sky touched down and went away again.

weapons.name: Stormglass Tether Lance of the Pyre-Tenders
weapons.description: Recovered from the Pyre-Tenders, still serviceable. Stormglass is fulgurite, dug up whole where the sky touched down and went away again.

weapons.name: Hoarlens Bone Orchard Spire Lance
weapons.description: Taken off a spire that was doing this on its own, to nobody, for years. A hoarlens is ground from lake ice that never got the message, and it grinds true. The Orchard was planted deliberately, and this was harvested from it the same way.

weapons.name: Hollowlight Siege Lance in Hoarlens
weapons.description: The siege lance pattern, as the Hollow of Lights understood it. A hoarlens is ground from lake ice that never got the message, and it grinds true.

weapons.name: Emberlens Cinder Flats Needle Lance
weapons.description: A emberlens needle lance, out of the Cinder Flats. Thin enough to be discourteous. The line it draws is barely there and goes all the way through.

weapons.name: Blightprism Ashen Reach Coil Lance
weapons.description: Wound from collar to tip, and it hums the whole time you are carrying it. Someone in the Ashen Reach thought blightprism would improve on that.

weapons.name: Blightprism Rift-Scar Tether Lance
weapons.description: Grounded to a spike you are supposed to drive in first. Nobody ever does. Taken out of the wound the light left going out. There is a name scratched under the grip, worn past reading.

weapons.name: Chorded Brass Bell-Ringer’s Spire Lance
weapons.description: The spire lance pattern, as the Bell-Ringers understood it. Chorded brass was cast to a pitch and it has not drifted, which after this long is a claim about the world.

weapons.name: Red Prism Mirefen Siege Lance
weapons.description: The fen takes one in ten of everything and gives back things like this. The red prism cuts before it burns. Nobody has satisfactorily explained the order.

weapons.name: Red Prism Needle Lance of the Nine Cairns
weapons.description: The red prism cuts before it burns. Nobody has satisfactorily explained the order. Made for the Nine Cairns, and outlived it comfortably.

weapons.name: Drawn Arcwire Coil Lance of the Sixth Hall
weapons.description: Drawn a hair at a time, over years, by people who could not be told why it had to be one piece. Made for the Sixth Hall, and outlived it comfortably.

weapons.name: Vigilkeep Tether Lance in Voidglass
weapons.description: Voidglass is what the Hollow of Lights leaves behind, and it is colder on the side away from you. Grounded to a spike you are supposed to drive in first. Nobody ever does. Nobody in the Vigilkeepers signed it.

weapons.name: Frostmarch Spire Lance in Voidglass
weapons.description: Taken off a spire that was doing this on its own, to nobody, for years. The season was pinned to the Frostmarch and never released; the steel remembers.

weapons.name: Fenwright Stormglass Coil Lance
weapons.description: Fenwright work: they keep nine parts and give the tenth to the water. Wound from collar to tip, and it hums the whole time you are carrying it.

weapons.name: Hoarlens Grey Strand Tether Lance
weapons.description: Sworn to the Slow Salt, whatever that was worth by the end. A hoarlens is ground from lake ice that never got the message, and it grinds true.

weapons.name: Hoarlens Hollow Court Spire Lance
weapons.description: The spire lance pattern, as the Hollow Court understood it. A hoarlens is ground from lake ice that never got the message, and it grinds true.

weapons.name: Sunken March Emberlens Siege Lance
weapons.description: Sworn to the Slow Tide, whatever that was worth by the end. An emberlens is fire-glass, and you can see the moment it was made trapped inside it.

weapons.name: Roadwarden’s Blightprism Needle Lance
weapons.description: Thin enough to be discourteous. The line it draws is barely there and goes all the way through. A blightprism grew in the water rather than being cut, and the light that leaves it has been somewhere. The rest is guesswork.

weapons.name: Blightprism Coil Lance of the Palewaste
weapons.description: Wound from collar to tip, and it hums the whole time you are carrying it. Salt where a capital was, and this was dug out of the salt. There is a name scratched under the grip, worn past reading.

weapons.name: Chorded Brass Tether Lance of the Turned Earth
weapons.description: Grounded to a spike you are supposed to drive in first. Nobody ever does. A graveward’s tool, and they were not fussy about which of its uses came first. There is a name scratched under the grip, worn past reading.

weapons.name: Red Prism Spire Lance of the Long Road
weapons.description: A spire lance in red prism, in the Hollowwood manner. Carried out of the Hollowwood by somebody who did not look back.

weapons.name: Red Prism Siege Lance of the Pyre-Tenders
weapons.description: Sworn to the Kept Flame, whatever that was worth by the end. The red prism cuts before it burns. Nobody has satisfactorily explained the order.

weapons.name: Drawn Arcwire Needle Lance of the Planted Dead
weapons.description: The Orchard was planted deliberately, and this was harvested from it the same way. Thin enough to be discourteous. The line it draws is barely there and goes all the way through.

weapons.name: Hollowlight Drawn Arcwire Coil Lance
weapons.description: A drawn arcwire coil lance, out of the Hollow of Lights. Wound from collar to tip, and it hums the whole time you are carrying it.

weapons.name: Cinder Flats Voidglass Tether Lance
weapons.description: Grounded to a spike you are supposed to drive in first. Nobody ever does. Every fire in the kingdom was lit from the Flats, including the one that made this.

weapons.name: Stormglass Ashen Reach Needle Lance
weapons.description: Recovered from the Ashen Reach, still serviceable. Stormglass is fulgurite, dug up whole where the sky touched down and went away again.

weapons.name: Stormglass Coil Lance of the Wound
weapons.description: Recovered from the Rift Scar, still serviceable. Stormglass is fulgurite, dug up whole where the sky touched down and went away again.

weapons.name: Hoarlens Tether Lance of the Held Note
weapons.description: A hoarlens tether lance, out of the Bell-Ringers. Grounded to a spike you are supposed to drive in first. Nobody ever does.

weapons.name: Mirefen Emberlens Spire Lance
weapons.description: The spire lance pattern, as the Mirefen understood it. An emberlens is fire-glass, and you can see the moment it was made trapped inside it.

weapons.name: Emberlens Cairnward Siege Lance
weapons.description: An emberlens is fire-glass, and you can see the moment it was made trapped inside it. Built to open a gate, and it has never been asked to do anything smaller.

weapons.name: Pale Choir Blightprism Needle Lance
weapons.description: Sworn to the Sixth Hall, whatever that was worth by the end. A blightprism grew in the water rather than being cut, and the light that leaves it has been somewhere.

weapons.name: Chorded Brass Coil Lance of the Vigilkeepers
weapons.description: A chorded brass coil lance, out of the Vigilkeepers. Wound from collar to tip, and it hums the whole time you are carrying it.

weapons.name: Frostmarch Chorded Brass Tether Lance
weapons.description: Grounded to a spike you are supposed to drive in first. Nobody ever does. Chorded brass was cast to a pitch and it has not drifted, which after this long is a claim about the world. The rest is guesswork.

weapons.name: Fenwright Spire Lance in Red Prism
weapons.description: Made in the Fenwrights, of red prism. Taken off a spire that was doing this on its own, to nobody, for years.

weapons.name: Drawn Arcwire Siege Lance of the Slow Salt
weapons.description: Built to open a gate, and it has never been asked to do anything smaller. Drawn a hair at a time, over years, by people who could not be told why it had to be one piece. Everything that floated came to the Strand and stopped, and this came with it.

weapons.name: Drawn Arcwire Needle Lance of the Abdication
weapons.description: Thin enough to be discourteous. The line it draws is barely there and goes all the way through. Someone in the Hollow Court thought drawn arcwire would improve on that.

weapons.name: Voidglass Coil Lance of the Slow Tide
weapons.description: Voidglass is what the Hollow of Lights leaves behind, and it is colder on the side away from you. Out of the province that agreed to go under and never came back up. It still balances.

weapons.name: Stormglass Roadwarden’s Siege Lance
weapons.description: Sworn to the Road Law, whatever that was worth by the end. Stormglass is fulgurite, dug up whole where the sky touched down and went away again.

weapons.name: Palewaste Needle Lance in Stormglass
weapons.description: Salt where a capital was, and this was dug out of the salt. Stormglass is fulgurite, dug up whole where the sky touched down and went away again. You can feel where the last owner held it.

weapons.name: Graveward Coil Lance in Hoarlens
weapons.description: A hoarlens coil lance, out of the Gravewards. Wound from collar to tip, and it hums the whole time you are carrying it.

armour.name: Roadwarden's Kettle Helm
armour.description: A wide brim, for rain. The rain is the least of it now.

armour.name: Roadwarden's Banded Coat
armour.description: Bands of kept iron over boiled hide. Repaired eleven times; the twelfth was refused.

armour.name: Roadwarden's Toll Gloves
armour.description: Palms worn smooth by a rope that no longer closes anything.

armour.name: Roadwarden's Marching Greaves
armour.description: Shin-plates dented from the inside, which is the harder trick.

armour.name: Pilgrim's Bound Hood
armour.description: Wound twice around the mouth, so the road cannot be argued with.

armour.name: Pilgrim's Grey Habit
armour.description: Undyed. Dye was a thing you bought in a town that still had a market.

armour.name: Pilgrim's Road-Worn Mantle
armour.description: Thin enough to see the weather through, which is its own kind of honesty.

armour.name: Strandpicker's Tarred Cap
armour.description: Tar keeps the salt out and the smell in. A fair trade, they said.

armour.name: Strandpicker's Salt-Cured Jerkin
armour.description: Stiff as a board until it is warm, and it is never warm.

armour.name: Strandpicker's Netting Wraps
armour.description: Fingers left free, because the tide does not wait for you to take your gloves off.

armour.name: Strandpicker's Wading Boots
armour.description: Filled with water on the first morning and never fully emptied.

armour.name: Lampbearer's Ashen Coif
armour.description: Soot has printed the shape of a lantern onto the left temple.

armour.name: Lampbearer's Wick-Stitched Robe
armour.description: Spare wick sewn into the hem, a yard of it, in case the night was long.

armour.name: Lampbearer's Guttering Cloak
armour.description: Scorched through in eleven places. Each one was somebody's doorway.

armour.name: Fen-Wife's Reed Veil
armour.description: Reeds cut at the third joint. Any other joint and the fen notices.

armour.name: Fen-Wife's Weeping Weeds
armour.description: Never dries. She said it was not supposed to.

armour.name: Fen-Wife's Tithe Gloves
armour.description: Stained to the wrist in a green that will not name itself.

armour.name: Ashen Marcher's Sallet
armour.description: The visor is fixed open. Whoever fixed it had reasons and did not write them down.

armour.name: Ashen Marcher's Grey Hauberk
armour.description: Ash in every ring. Beating it out only makes more room for ash.

armour.name: Ashen Marcher's Cinder Gauntlets
armour.description: Warm to hold, long after the last fire they touched.

armour.name: Ashen Marcher's Levelled Greaves
armour.description: Cut short at the knee for wading a country that is all one depth.

armour.name: Orchard Warden's Barred Helm
armour.description: Bars close enough that nothing gets in. Nothing much gets out either.

armour.name: Orchard Warden's Rooted Cuirass
armour.description: Root-marks under the lacquer, growing in the direction of the heart.

armour.name: Orchard Warden's Pruning Gauntlets
armour.description: Shears were standard issue. So was the instruction not to count.

armour.name: Orchard Warden's Planted Greaves
armour.description: Heavy at the heel, for standing very still in soft ground.

armour.name: Tithe-Taker's Ledger Hood
armour.description: A slot at the temple for a stylus. The stylus is long gone; the habit is not.

armour.name: Tithe-Taker's Counting Coat
armour.description: Nine inner pockets, each labelled in a hand that grew smaller every year.

armour.name: Tithe-Taker's Debtor's Cloak
armour.description: Turned inside out, because the outside was owed to someone.

armour.name: Drowned Oath Great Helm
armour.description: Full-faced, and the eye-slit silted up. They did not open it to march.

armour.name: Drowned Oath Cuirass
armour.description: Still holds a pint of the march inside the breastplate. It will not pour out.

armour.name: Drowned Oath Gauntlets
armour.description: Fingers curled around the memory of a haft.

armour.name: Drowned Oath Sabatons
armour.description: Weighted at the sole. On purpose. They meant to stay down.

armour.name: Drowned Oath Standard
armour.description: Worn as a cape when there was no longer a pole worth raising.

armour.name: Sixth Hall Choir Mask
armour.description: No mouth-hole. The singing was never done with the mouth.

armour.name: Sixth Hall Vestment
armour.description: White once. White is a colour you have to keep paying for.

armour.name: Sixth Hall Bell-Ringer's Wraps
armour.description: Rope-burn set into the linen, a permanent record of a permanent duty.

armour.name: Sixth Hall Silence Mantle
armour.description: Heavy at the shoulders, to teach the wearer not to turn quickly.

armour.name: Vigilkeeper's Slotted Helm
armour.description: Slotted for hearing, not for seeing. That was the job.

armour.name: Vigilkeeper's Long Hauberk
armour.description: Down to the knee, so a man could sleep standing and not feel the cold at his back.

armour.name: Vigilkeeper's Standing Greaves
armour.description: Worn through at the back of the calf, from leaning on the same wall.

armour.name: Cinderwright's Forge Helm
armour.description: A hood of plate with a smoke-slot. The smoke still finds the eyes.

armour.name: Cinderwright's Slag Plate
armour.description: Poured, not beaten. It is a little wrong everywhere and perfect nowhere.

armour.name: Cinderwright's Quenching Gauntlets
armour.description: Held things that were white. The palms remember which parts.

armour.name: Cinderwright's Ash-Banked Greaves
armour.description: Banked with ash inside, the way you bank a fire you mean to find again.

armour.name: Saltcrown Circlet Helm
armour.description: A circlet welded to a helm by someone who could not decide which was the lie.

armour.name: Saltcrown Coat of Plates
armour.description: Court velvet over kept iron. The velvet went first.

armour.name: Saltcrown Court Gauntlets
armour.description: Etched for presentation. Sharpened at the knuckle for the other thing.

armour.name: Saltcrown Chancel Greaves
armour.description: Made for kneeling and standing again, in that order, in front of witnesses.

armour.name: Frostmarch Sentinel's Visor
armour.description: Frozen shut in the down position. It has been useful exactly once.

armour.name: Frostmarch Sentinel's Rimed Plate
armour.description: The rime is structural now. Chip it and the plate goes with it.

armour.name: Frostmarch Sentinel's Frozen Gauntlets
armour.description: Will not fully open. You learn to grip things the way they let you.

armour.name: Frostmarch Sentinel's Pinned Greaves
armour.description: Pinned at the knee, so the leg locks straight when the wearer stops thinking.

armour.name: Frostmarch Sentinel's Frost-Stiff Cape
armour.description: Hangs like a board. In a wind it does not move at all, which unsettles people.

armour.name: Riftwalker's Split Mask
armour.description: Two halves that do not quite meet. You see slightly more than there is.

armour.name: Riftwalker's Seamed Coat
armour.description: The seams run where no seam should. They are warm on one side only.

armour.name: Riftwalker's Thin Wraps
armour.description: Almost nothing. Almost nothing is the point.

armour.name: Riftwalker's Unravelling Cloak
armour.description: Losing a thread a day. It has been losing a thread a day for a very long time.

armour.name: Wanderer's Motley
armour.description: Four fabrics, four owners, one thread. The thread is the wearer.

armour.name: Wanderer's Patched Cloak
armour.description: The patches outnumber the cloak. At some point that stops being a repair.

armour.name: Hollowlight Crown
armour.description: Not metal. It holds its shape the way a held breath does.

armour.name: Hollowlight Vestment
armour.description: Lit from inside by nothing you can point at.

armour.name: Hollowlight Cradling Gloves
armour.description: Cupped, always, as though about to be given something.

armour.name: Hollowlight Wading Hose
armour.description: For standing in the fall of it without being carried off.

armour.name: Hollowlight Falling Mantle
armour.description: Falls further than the body it hangs on. It has been measured; it is not an illusion.

armour.name: Husk-Bitten Cap
armour.description: Taken off something that had stopped needing a head.

armour.name: Cracked Field Helm
armour.description: A crack from crown to brow, filled with candle wax by an optimist.

armour.name: Beggar's Wrappings
armour.description: Twelve yards of linen and no shirt underneath. It is warmer than it looks.

armour.name: Woodsman's Jerkin
armour.description: Elbow patches sewn on from the inside, which is how you know he did it himself.

armour.name: Tollhouse Mitts
armour.description: Fingerless, for counting. There is nothing left to count.

armour.name: Split Trousers of the Verge
armour.description: Split to the knee for wading. The wading never stopped.

armour.name: Tattered Road Cloak
armour.description: Grey on grey, so the road cannot pick you out from it.

armour.name: Driftwood Bracers
armour.description: Slats of sea-bleached wood, bound with gut. Light, and they float.

armour.name: Kelp-Wound Boots
armour.description: The kelp dried hard and then dried harder. Nothing gets through.

armour.name: Gull-Feather Cape
armour.description: Weighs nothing, and the wind treats you like it treats a bird.

armour.name: Fenwatcher's Wide Hat
armour.description: Wide enough to keep the fen's opinion off your face.

armour.name: Mirefen Waders
armour.description: Sealed at the thigh. Whatever gets in stays in with you.

armour.name: Rotwarden's Plastron
armour.description: Rings tinned against the green. The tin has begun to lose the argument.

armour.name: Ashfall Half-Helm
armour.description: Open at the jaw so a man can be understood when he gives the order.

armour.name: Grave-Digger's Apron
armour.description: Hide, doubled, and stained in a gradient that reads like a calendar.

armour.name: Orchard Rope Gloves
armour.description: Rope-palmed. The orchard is climbed more often than it is walked.

armour.name: Cairnkeeper's Hood
armour.description: Stone dust in every fold. He built nine hundred and stopped counting at four.

armour.name: Sunken March Sabatons
armour.description: Heavier than the man above them. That was the design brief.

armour.name: Silt-Filled Gauntlets
armour.description: Full of the province, packed hard. Nobody has managed to empty them.

armour.name: Drowned Standard-Bearer's Cape
armour.description: Mail-backed, for a man expected to be shot at from behind.

armour.name: Choirless Mask
armour.description: The seventh hall's mask. It was never issued, because the seventh never sang.

armour.name: Bell-Founder's Apron
armour.description: Spark-burns in a spray pattern, radiating from the heart outward.

armour.name: Cinder Flats Stormcoat
armour.description: For the days the flats blow. Every day is a day the flats blow.

armour.name: Emberpicker's Gloves
armour.description: Thin, deliberately. You cannot pick an ember you cannot feel.

armour.name: Slagwalker's Greaves
armour.description: Soles poured fresh each season, over the last season's soles.

armour.name: Saltbitten Mantle
armour.description: Salt has eaten holes in a pattern that looks almost like writing.

armour.name: Palewaste Regent's Circlet
armour.description: Worn by a regent for a king who was, at the time, a rumour.

armour.name: Chair-Keeper's Plate
armour.description: He guarded an empty chair for thirty years and considered it a posting.

armour.name: Frost-Pinned Hood
armour.description: Pinned shut with a splinter of the season itself.

armour.name: Frostmarch Trapper's Mitts
armour.description: Fur turned inward. The animal is still, in some sense, doing its job.

armour.name: Nightsworn Gauntlets
armour.description: Blackened by a process the smith would only describe as 'patience'.

armour.name: Rift-Scarred Half-Plate
armour.description: Half of it came back. The armourer would not say from where.

armour.name: Unlit Lantern-Cloak
armour.description: Hooks all down the inside for lanterns. None of them are lit. None of them will be.

armour.name: Hollow-of-Lights Sabatons
armour.description: They leave prints that stay bright for a count of four.

armour.name: Pilgrim's Wound Wrappings
armour.description: Wound from the hem of the habit. The habit is shorter every year.

armour.name: Lampbearer's Oil-Stained Mitts
armour.description: The right one is burnt through at the thumb, from pinching wicks.

armour.name: Fen-Wife's Dripping Shawl
armour.description: Hung on the door for a hundred years and never once finished drying.

armour.name: Tithe-Taker's Stylus Gloves
armour.description: Cut away at two fingertips, so a figure could be felt as well as read.

armour.name: Vigilkeeper's Bell-Rope Gauntlets
armour.description: Palms worn smooth by a rope that pulled nothing for thirty years.

armour.name: Wanderer's Mismatched Hood
armour.description: Two hoods, cut in half and sewn back together the wrong way round.

armour.name: Wanderer's Odd Gloves
armour.description: A pair only in the sense that there are two of them.

armour.name: Barrow-Sworn Sallet
armour.description: Sworn over an open grave, and never taken off above one since.

armour.name: Barrow-Sworn Hauberk
armour.description: Every ring closed by hand, by men who counted while they worked.

armour.name: Barrow-Sworn Diggers
armour.description: Reinforced across the back of the hand, where a spade sits.

armour.name: Barrow-Sworn Chausses
armour.description: Mud to the knee that will not come out, and is not entirely mud.

armour.name: Barrow-Sworn Shroud-Cloak
armour.description: Cut from a shroud that was measured for somebody taller.

armour.name: Hollow Court Attendant Helm
armour.description: Full-faced, because the court preferred not to be looked at directly.

armour.name: Hollow Court Cuirass
armour.description: Polished on the inside as carefully as the out. Nobody has explained why.

armour.name: Hollow Court Presenting Gauntlets
armour.description: Made for holding a cup out at arm's length for a very long time.

armour.name: Hollow Court Standing Greaves
armour.description: The court stood. There were chairs; standing was the point of them.

armour.name: Hollow Court Mantle of Attendance
armour.description: Weighted at the hem so it hangs correctly whatever the wearer does.

armour.name: UNCLASSIFIED — Crown
armour.description: The catalogue has a number for it and nothing else. The number is not ours.

armour.name: UNCLASSIFIED — Carapace
armour.description: Warm. It was warm when it was found, and it has not cooled since.

armour.name: UNCLASSIFIED — Manifolds
armour.description: Six fingers of room in each. You are not obliged to fill them.

armour.name: UNCLASSIFIED — Struts
armour.description: They take the first step slightly before you decide to.

armour.name: UNCLASSIFIED — Trailing Field
armour.description: Not cloth. It hangs like cloth out of what seems to be politeness.

armourSets.name: Roadwarden's Kit
armourSets.description: Issued to men who were told the road would be reopened within the season.

bonuses.text: The road still knows you. +4% physical negation.
The Road Law is yours to speak.

armourSets.name: Verge Pilgrim's Grey
armourSets.description: Nobody agreed on where the pilgrimage ended. They walked anyway.

bonuses.text: Nothing to carry, nowhere to be. +2 Will.
You have learned the Hound's Line.
The road ends where you stop walking. +2 Will, +4% spirit negation.

armourSets.name: Strandpicker's Salt
armourSets.description: Everything that floated came here. Someone had to sort it.

bonuses.text: You may hold a Steady Hand.

armourSets.name: Lampbearer's Wick
armourSets.description: They were paid in oil. When the oil stopped, most of them kept walking the route.

bonuses.text: Oil enough for one more night. +6% fire negation, +2 Faith.

armourSets.name: Fen-Wife's Weeds
armourSets.description: One in ten of everything, and no receipts. The fen kept its own books.

bonuses.text: The water is on your side. +9% rot negation.
The Fen-Thorn Fence rises where you ask.
One in ten of everything, and the fen counts you as paid. +7% rot negation, +2 Faith.

armourSets.name: Ashen Marcher's Grey
armourSets.description: Grey, and level, and much deeper than it looks. So were they.

armourSets.name: Orchard Warden's Plate
armourSets.description: It was planted deliberately. Someone was paid to keep it tidy.

bonuses.text: The Warden's Answer is yours to give.

armourSets.name: Tithe-Taker's Leathers
armourSets.description: He kept perfect books for a kingdom that had stopped existing.

bonuses.text: Books closed on a kingdom that stopped reading them. +5% damage, +4% bleed negation.

armourSets.name: Drowned Oath
armourSets.description: A province agreed to go under. The garrison agreed with it.

bonuses.text: The oath holds the body up. +3 Vigor, +2 Endurance.
The Pinning Oath is yours to swear.

armourSets.name: Vestments of the Sixth Hall
armourSets.description: Seven halls, six of them singing. The sixth sang loudest and stopped first.

bonuses.text: The Hymn of the Sixth Hall is yours.

armourSets.name: Vigilkeeper's Mail
armourSets.description: Three watches a night, every night, for a bell that had already been taken down.

bonuses.text: Awake at the wrong hour. +5% physical negation.
The Iron Vigil is yours to keep.
Three watches a night, and the fourth is yours. +5% physical negation, +2 Endurance.

armourSets.name: Cinderwright's Plate
armourSets.description: Every fire in the kingdom was lit from here, and they kept the ledger of that too.

armourSets.name: Saltcrown Regalia
armourSets.description: Salt where a capital was, and a chair nobody sat in. The court dressed for it regardless.

bonuses.text: The King's Measure is yours to take.

armourSets.name: Frostmarch Sentinel
armourSets.description: The season was pinned here and never released. Somebody had to hold the pin.

bonuses.text: The Winter Temper is yours to take on.

armourSets.name: Riftwalker's Seams
armourSets.description: Made by cutting a coat in half and asking the wound to hold the halves together.

armourSets.name: Wanderer's Motley
armourSets.description: Assembled from four dead men's wardrobes and worn without apology.

bonuses.text: Three dead men agree on you. +1 to every attribute.
A wardrobe with nobody left to object. +1 to every attribute, +4% damage.

armourSets.name: Hollowlight Vestments
armourSets.description: Where it fell, and where it is still falling. They dressed to catch it.

bonuses.text: You may Hold the Light In.

mounts.name: Ashen Elk
mounts.description: It was grazing the burn line when the world went quiet, and it never stopped. Steady, patient, and entirely unbothered by you — it walks the ash roads like they are still fields.

acquire.note: The elk lowers its head. It has been waiting for someone to be tired enough.

mounts.name: Pale Hound
mounts.description: Too long in the leg and too quick in the eye. The choir's keeper sells its lead, not its loyalty — it runs until you make it stop, and it will not carry a coward.

acquire.note: The hound takes the souls out of the bowl before it takes you.

mounts.name: Cinder Ram
mounts.description: Slowest of the four and certain about everything. It crossed the flats when they were still burning, and it has not hurried since — nothing you meet will convince it to start.

acquire.note: The ram considers the offering, then considers you, and finds both acceptable.

mounts.name: Rift Stag
mounts.description: Its antlers hold a seam of somewhere else. Ground goes by faster than it should, and so, quietly, does everything else — do not ask it where the missing steps go.

acquire.note: The stag steps out of a gap in the air that was not there a moment ago.

mounts.name: Fen Strider
mounts.description: Legs like wading poles and no opinion at all about what is under the water. Mud, peat and reed are all the same road to it, and it holds its pace across ground that takes a walker to the knee.

acquire.note: The strider walks out of standing water without once looking down.

mounts.name: Ash Hart
mounts.description: Bred thin and fast on the tending-walks, and nervous with it. It will outrun anything on the flats and put you down for a scratch, so ride it the way it is meant to be ridden: away.

acquire.note: The tender takes the souls, unties the hart, and steps well back.

mounts.name: Crag Goat
mounts.description: Slow, sour and impossible to shift. It picks its way across rime and scree at the same unhurried rate it picks its way across everything else, and a blow that would unseat you off anything else only annoys it.

acquire.note: The goat is handed over on a short rope, with condolences.

mounts.name: Spectral Steed
mounts.description: It was not here before you put the Seraph down, and it will not explain where it was. Fastest thing that will carry a rider, and the only one that never tires, because tiring is a thing bodies do.

acquire.note: The steed was already standing here. It has been, since the Seraph fell.

bosses.name: The Ashen Warden
bosses.title: Keeper of a Road That Ended

phases.banner: THE ASHEN WARDEN — Keeper of a Road That Ended
He remembers what the road was for.

bosses.epitaph: He was told to keep the road. Nobody told him the far end had been swallowed, and nobody came to relieve him, and a Warden does not abandon a post to go and check.

bosses.name: The Mirelord
bosses.title: Who Took One in Ten

phases.banner: THE MIRELORD — Who Took One in Ten
The water rises to meet him.
He is calling in what he is owed.

bosses.epitaph: The fen never asked for a lord. It asked for a ledger, and he volunteered, and for a long while the arithmetic was the only law anyone out here could rely on.

bosses.name: The Choir of Bells
bosses.title: Seven Voices, One Throat

phases.banner: THE CHOIR OF BELLS — Seven Voices, One Throat
The second voice joins. It was never far.
All seven, and none of them in tune.

bosses.epitaph: Six bells for the dead and one for the living, and when there were no living left the seventh was simply never rung. It has been holding the note ever since, waiting for someone to be worth it.

bosses.name: The First Flame Knight
bosses.title: Who Was Not Told to Stop

phases.banner: THE FIRST FLAME KNIGHT — Who Was Not Told to Stop
He sets the sword down. He picks it back up, lit.
The order stands. The order has always stood.

bosses.epitaph: Every fire in the kingdom was lit from his. When the kingdom stopped needing fires he kept the first one anyway, because no order arrived cancelling the first one, and he was a man who read his orders carefully.

bosses.name: The Hollow King
bosses.title: Who Would Not Sit

phases.banner: THE HOLLOW KING — Who Would Not Sit
He removes the crown. It stays where it was.
Abdication, at last, and in the only form left to him.

bosses.epitaph: He said a crown was only a promise you could take off, and then he did not take it off, and then he could not, and then there was nothing under it that remembered making the promise.

bosses.name: The Frostbound Colossus
bosses.title: Anchor of a Season

phases.banner: THE FROSTBOUND COLOSSUS — Anchor of a Season
Something under the ice takes the weight off him.
Winter has not moved in a very long time. It moves now.

bosses.epitaph: It was set here to hold the season still while the rest was put right. The rest was not put right. It has been holding a page open for a book nobody came back to finish reading.

bosses.name: The Rift Seraph
bosses.title: That Which Came Through Sideways

phases.banner: THE RIFT SERAPH — That Which Came Through Sideways
It is standing in two places. Neither is here.
It has stopped pretending to have a shape.

bosses.epitaph: It did not come to conquer, or to judge, or to answer. It came through the hole the Spirit left when it broke, the way weather comes through a broken window, and it has no more opinion of us than weather does.

bosses.name: The Bright Spirit
bosses.title: What Is Left of the Light

phases.banner: THE BRIGHT SPIRIT — What Is Left of the Light
Every shard you carried is answering at once.
It is trying to become whole through you. Do not let go.

attacks.name: Seven Ways to Hold a Light

bosses.epitaph: It was never a god. It was a light, and lights do not intend anything, and it broke the way a lamp breaks — without malice, without warning, and taking the room with it. Everything since has been people arguing about whose fault the dark is.

bosses.name: The Stone Shepherd
bosses.title: Who Counts the Ring

phases.banner: THE STONE SHEPHERD — Who Counts the Ring
One of them is missing. He begins again.

bosses.epitaph: He was set to keep the count of the ring and has kept it, aloud, without pause, since the eighteenth stone stopped being there. The arithmetic is the only part of him left that still works.

bosses.name: The Forge Tyrant
bosses.title: Who Would Not Let It Out

phases.banner: THE FORGE TYRANT — Who Would Not Let It Out
He works the bellows with the other hand.
The pour, and nothing to pour it into.

bosses.epitaph: The order was to keep the forge lit until relieved. He read it as a prohibition on ever letting anything out of it, including the fire, including himself, and he has been consistent about that ever since.

bosses.name: The Barrow Maw
bosses.title: What the Pit Grew Instead

phases.banner: THE BARROW MAW — What the Pit Grew Instead
It brings up what it was given.

bosses.epitaph: Nobody planted it. Enough was put into the ground in one place, for long enough, that the ground developed an opinion about being fed, and then a mouth, and then a preference.

bosses.name: The Warden of the Kept Stile
bosses.title: Elite of the Grey Strand

phases.banner: THE WARDEN OF THE KEPT STILE — Elite of the Grey Strand
It stops pacing itself.

bosses.epitaph: He kept a gate in a fence that fell down a hundred years ago, and he kept it well, and he kept it alone.

bosses.name: The Tithe-Collector
bosses.title: Elite of the Mirefen

phases.banner: THE TITHE-COLLECTOR — Elite of the Mirefen
It stops pacing itself.

bosses.epitaph: She still counts what the water owes her, and the water still pays, and neither of them can stop.

bosses.name: The Gravewright
bosses.title: Elite of the Bone Orchard

phases.banner: THE GRAVEWRIGHT — Elite of the Bone Orchard
It stops pacing itself.

bosses.epitaph: He dug every row of them himself, and he is not finished, and he has begun to look at the living as unplanted ground.

bosses.name: The Last Dry Sergeant
bosses.title: Elite of the Sunken March

phases.banner: THE LAST DRY SERGEANT — Elite of the Sunken March
It stops pacing itself.

bosses.epitaph: The order to fall back was given. It was given to a room that was already underwater, and he has not heard it yet.

bosses.name: The Bell-Keeper of the Sixth Hall
bosses.title: Elite of the Pale Choir

phases.banner: THE BELL-KEEPER OF THE SIXTH HALL — Elite of the Pale Choir
It stops pacing itself.

bosses.epitaph: Six halls, six bells, six keepers. Five of them stopped ringing when the choir did. This one did not notice.

bosses.name: The Cinderwright Foreman
bosses.title: Elite of the Cinder Flats

phases.banner: THE CINDERWRIGHT FOREMAN — Elite of the Cinder Flats
It stops pacing itself.

bosses.epitaph: Every shift he counted his crew out, and every shift he counted them back, and the number has not matched in a long time.

bosses.name: The Saltcrown Pretender
bosses.title: Elite of the Palewaste

phases.banner: THE SALTCROWN PRETENDER — Elite of the Palewaste
It stops pacing itself.

bosses.epitaph: He crowned himself in a country with nobody left to object, which is the only way anyone has ever managed it.

bosses.name: Herald of the Long Winter
bosses.title: Elite of the Frostmarch

phases.banner: HERALD OF THE LONG WINTER — Elite of the Frostmarch
It stops pacing itself.

bosses.epitaph: It walks ahead of the cold the way a page walks ahead of a king, and it has been walking for a very long time.

items.name: Ashlight Flask
items.description: A finger of light kept in glass. It was drawn from a shard, once, by someone who is no longer available to explain how.

items.name: Deep Ashlight Flask
items.description: Drawn from nearer the centre of the shard, where the light is thicker and less willing.

items.name: Stillwater Flask
items.description: Water taken from under ice, where nothing has moved for long enough to settle. Drinking it settles you the same way.

items.name: Deep Stillwater Flask
items.description: Colder. Quieter. Drinkers report a brief, unwelcome clarity about the state of things.

items.name: Flask Charge
items.description: A pinch of glassed light. Add it to a flask and the flask holds one more draught, which is not the same as holding more light.

items.name: Vessel Seed
items.description: Grown in the throat of a shrine bell. It teaches a flask to carry a heavier draught. Nobody has explained what it grows into if you leave it alone.

items.name: Rotwort Sprig
items.description: It grows only in water that has already killed something. The Mirefen provides generously.

items.name: Hearthsalt
items.description: Scraped from the floor of a hearth that burned for two hundred years. Held in the mouth, it argues with the cold.

items.name: Bloodmoss Wad
items.description: Packed into a wound, it stops the bleeding by taking an interest in it.

items.name: Quietwater Draught
items.description: For when the light in you starts speaking with somebody else's cadence. Drink it early. Drinking it late is only politeness.

items.name: Ironbind Tonic
items.description: Tastes of nails. Stiffens the stance for a short while, and the jaw for rather longer.

items.name: Longbreath Tonic
items.description: Brewed by a hermit who had run out of everything except time and lungs.

items.name: Cinder Resin
items.description: Smear it on a blade and the blade remembers a forge it never came from.

items.name: Gravebite Resin
items.description: Ground from the teeth of things that were buried with their mouths open.

items.name: Frostbind Resin
items.description: Kept in a stoppered horn. If the horn is warm, it has already been wasted.

items.name: Wornstone
items.description: Any rock a hundred people have sharpened something on. It has learned the shape of an edge and gives it back cheaply.

items.name: Kept Iron
items.description: Iron from a tool somebody maintained for their whole life. It takes an upgrade well, out of habit.

items.name: Named Ash
items.description: Ash from a pyre where somebody said the name aloud. It is measurably heavier than ash from a pyre where nobody did.

items.name: Oathglass
items.description: Sand fused by a promise breaking at speed. Sharp on every face, including the ones facing inward.

items.name: Remembered Ember
items.description: It has not been hot for a very long time and is still, unmistakably, an ember.

items.name: Spiritbound Shard
items.description: A splinter of the Bright Spirit small enough to be useful. There is no such thing as a splinter of it small enough to be safe.

items.name: Remembrance of the Long Watch
items.description: The Warden's shard, still keeping something. Hold it and you can hear boots on a road that is under forty feet of ash.

items.name: Remembrance of the Slow Tide
items.description: Wet to the touch in any weather. Counting things while holding it becomes unpleasantly easy.

items.name: Remembrance of the Seventh Voice
items.description: It is silent, and the silence has a shape, and the shape is a note that has been held too long to end gracefully.

items.name: Remembrance of the Kept Flame
items.description: Warm. It has been warm since before anyone alive was born, and shows no sign of considering the matter closed.

items.name: Remembrance of the Empty Chair
items.description: The weight of a crown without the crown. Set it down and you will notice you are still standing as though wearing it.

items.name: Remembrance of the Long Winter
items.description: It does not melt. It does not chill the hand either. It simply holds its own weather, politely, at arm's length from yours.

items.name: Remembrance of the Sideways Door
items.description: Looked at directly it is a stone. Looked at from the corner of the eye it is an opening, and something in it is not looking back, which is worse.

items.name: Remembrance of the Light Itself
items.description: The last shard, and the first. Everything else in the world is a piece of this that got lost on the way somewhere.

items.name: Remembrance of the Counted Ring
items.description: It keeps a total. Carry it a day and you will know, without ever having looked, exactly how many things are in the room with you — and that the number is one short, and has been for longer than you have been alive.

items.name: Remembrance of the Long Pit
items.description: Heavier at the bottom of a pack than at the top, whichever way up you put it. Everything you carry beside it comes out a little warmer and a little less yours, which is what the ground has been doing to the orchard for a hundred years, only slower.

items.name: Remembrance of the Kept Pour
items.description: Hot through cloth, through leather, through the flat of a hand. It is not giving off heat. It is refusing to, the way he refused, and a refusal that old has to go somewhere.

items.name: Warden's Road-Token
items.description: Handed out to anyone who agreed to walk a stretch of road and come back. Most of them came back.

items.name: Fen Ledger Seal
items.description: One in ten, marked in a hand that never blotted once. Whoever kept these books did not sleep and did not need to.

items.name: Clapper of a Cracked Bell
items.description: The bell it belonged to could not finish its note. This finishes other things instead.

items.name: Ember Locket
items.description: Worn against the sternum by the pyre-tenders, so that if they went out, at least something of theirs did not.

items.name: Splinter of the Empty Chair
items.description: Taken from a throne nobody sat in. It confers no authority whatsoever, and a great deal of stubbornness.

items.name: Anchor-Ring of Nine Winters
items.description: Cold enough that the hand forgets it after a minute. That forgetting is the point.

items.name: Quiet Pair
items.description: Two small weights on one cord, balanced so exactly that they make no sound against each other. Ever.

items.name: Vesselborn Lantern
items.description: Empty. It was always empty. You are what it was built to hold, and it has been waiting with the patience of glass.

items.name: Catacomb Iron Key
items.description: Every catacomb in the kingdom used the same lock, on the theory that nobody would want in. The theory was sound for a century.

items.name: Choir Pass
items.description: A strip of lead stamped with a note. Held to the door of the Pale Choir, it argues successfully.
