items.name: Rift Sigil
items.description: Not a key. A shape the Rift finds familiar enough to let pass, the way a dog lets a coat through because it smells right.

items.name: Beacon Lens
items.description: Ground from a single sheet of oathglass. Slot it into a dead beacon and the beacon remembers where the others are.

items.name: Grave Offering
items.description: Coins, a comb, a knuckle of bread. Left for someone who has not needed any of it in a long time and would still notice its absence.

items.name: The Warden's Ledger
items.description: Two hundred years of road reports in one hand, then a different hand, then the first hand again. The last entry reads: ROAD CLEAR. NOTHING PASSED. NOTHING WILL.

items.name: Tithe Tally-Stick
items.description: Notched in tens. Every tenth notch is cut deeper and given a name. The names run out well before the notches do.

items.name: Psalter of the Pale Choir
items.description: Seven parts. The seventh is blank, with an instruction at the top: SING WHEN THERE IS SOMEONE LEFT TO SING TO.

items.name: The King's Last Writ
items.description: An abdication, correctly witnessed, correctly sealed, never delivered. The messenger is still in the corridor, in a manner of speaking.

items.name: Rite of the Vesselborn
items.description: Instructions for making a person who can hold a shard without going out. Step one is a child. Step four is a promise. Step nine has been scratched through by every hand that ever read it.

items.name: Otherworldly Ichor
items.description: Sold by the litre by something that does not appear to produce it. Cold going down, colder afterwards, and the focus it gives back is measurably more than a body that size should hold.

items.name: A Measure of the Rift
items.description: A weight with no side that faces you. The merchant sells them by count rather than by mass, which it says is the only honest way, and it says it in the tone of somebody correcting you.

items.name: The Unlit Lamp
items.description: A small house lamp, brass gone brown, wick trimmed square by a century of the same hand. It has one burn left in it. It is not for the road. It is for after the road.

items.name: Pilgrim's Loaf
items.description: Baked hard enough to keep for a month and eaten in about the same time. Every wayhouse on the road made it identically, which is how you know they all learned it from one bakery nobody can now point to.

items.name: Marrow Broth
items.description: Boiled from bones that were already boiled once. The second pass takes longer and gives back less, and the people who drink it have stopped expecting otherwise.

items.name: Saltfish Ration
items.description: Strand fare. Salt enough to keep it, salt enough to make you walk to the next water, which the wreckers considered a feature rather than a fault.

items.name: Hearth Stew
items.description: Kept on the same hook over the same fire for so long that nobody can name a single thing in it. It has been added to more often than it has been eaten, which is one definition of a home.

items.name: Black Honeycomb
items.description: The orchard bees kept working after the orchard stopped being an orchard. What they bring back is dark, and slow, and settles the head the way a long argument finally settling does.

items.name: Surefoot Tonic
items.description: Brewed for couriers who had to cross the fen at night. It does nothing for the fen. It does a great deal for the part of you that keeps checking where your feet are.

items.name: Soulhunger Tincture
items.description: Drunk before a fight by people who intended to be paid for it. The light in the dead leans toward you for a while, which is either a kindness or a habit it learned from something worse.

items.name: Emberwort Sprig
items.description: It grows on the cool side of a burn scar and nowhere else, so finding it means the fire has finished with that ground. Chewed, it tells the fire in you the same news.

items.name: Stormsalt
items.description: Scraped off the inside of a bell that was struck by lightning and went on ringing for a day and a half. It takes the jump out of a limb that has forgotten whose it is.

items.name: Stillmark Resin
items.description: Bled from a tree that grew through a shrine floor and kept the shrine's manners. On an edge it makes the cut quieter, and the quiet is what does the harm.

items.name: Ember Draught
items.description: Poured into a flask that has already been deepened once. The glass does not get bigger; the draught inside simply stops agreeing that it should stop.

items.name: Tidewrack Salt
items.description: Panned off the strand where the wrecks come apart. Every grain of it has been through a hull, a hold and a cargo, and it sharpens steel with the grudge of all three.

items.name: Pyre Clinker
items.description: What is left in the grate when a tending-fire has done its whole job. Hard, light, and quite unwilling to burn a second time, which is exactly what a temper wants.

items.name: Bellbronze Scrap
items.description: Cut from a bell that cracked rather than be melted for coin. Worked into an edge it keeps a note somewhere under the steel — not audible, exactly, but the wielder always knows it is there.

items.name: Gravefrost
items.description: Frost off the underside of a lid, in a season with no frost in it. It weighs a little more than the water it came from, and the difference has to have come from somewhere.

items.name: Coin from a Drowned Purse
items.description: Struck in a reign nobody at the crossroads can name. Still round, still stamped, still worth something to a merchant who does not ask which sea it was standing in.

items.name: Ninefold Button
items.description: Nine holes, one thread, sewn onto a coat by someone counting. Tithesmen paid well for these once, and the habit of paying outlived the reason for it.

items.name: The Tollman's Ring
items.description: Too big for any finger it has been found on. Every tollhouse on the road had one, and every one of them is described in the ledgers as the same ring.

items.name: A Glass Eye, Slightly Warm
items.description: Ground in the Palewaste, where they ground everything. Set it down in a cold room and come back: it is the temperature of a face. Collectors pay for it and do not keep it.

items.name: Seal of the Tollward Sentry
items.description: Pressed lead on a broken cord, taken off a sentry who was still standing his post two hundred years after the post stopped being anywhere. The stamp reads PAID. It is the only honest thing left on that stretch of road.

items.name: Ear-Cup of the Sixth Hall
items.description: Bronze, thin as a leaf, worn by the one who had to stand nearest the bell and count. Held to the ear now it gives back a hall you have not been in, and a number, and the number is always the same one.

items.name: Root-Crown of the Ninth Row
items.description: A knot of orchard root grown in a perfect circle around something the diggers left in place. The gravewright wore it. Nobody has established whether the root made the shape or was taught it.

items.name: Pennant of the Long Winter
items.description: Frozen mid-snap, and it has stayed mid-snap through a hundred still days. The herald carried it ahead of a season that never arrived, and the cloth is apparently still waiting for the wind it was promised.

items.name: Riftglass Thorn
items.description: A splinter off the Scar with a point at both ends and no middle that a hand can find. Wrapped, carried and sold on quickly by everyone who has ever owned one, which is the only recorded use.

regions.name: The Hollowwood Verge
regions.subtitle: Where the road still pretends to go somewhere

landmarks.name: The Hanging Tree at Nine Elms

regions.name: The Grey Strand
regions.subtitle: Everything that floated came here, and stopped

regions.name: The Mirefen
regions.subtitle: One in ten of everything, and no receipts

regions.name: The Ashen Reach
regions.subtitle: Grey, and level, and much deeper than it looks

regions.name: The Bone Orchard
regions.subtitle: It was planted deliberately, which is the worst part

regions.name: The Sunken March
regions.subtitle: A province that agreed to go under and never came back up

regions.name: The Pale Choir
regions.subtitle: Seven halls, six of them singing

regions.name: The Cinder Flats
regions.subtitle: Every fire in the kingdom was lit from here

regions.name: The Palewaste
regions.subtitle: Salt where a capital was, and a chair nobody sat in

regions.name: The Frostmarch
regions.subtitle: The season was pinned here and never released

regions.name: The Rift Scar
regions.subtitle: The wound the light left going out

regions.name: The Hollow of Lights
regions.subtitle: Where it fell, and where it is still falling

lore.title: Scratched Into a Doorframe
lore.text: WE WENT SOUTH. IF YOU ARE READING THIS WE DID NOT GET THERE. TAKE THE BLANKETS. LEAVE THE BOOK.

lore.title: Shrine Plaque, Half Legible
lore.text: Kneel if it helps. It does not listen and it does not judge, and of those two facts the second is the kindness.

lore.title: The Obelisks
lore.text: One hundred and nine were raised to mark where the light fell thickest. Ninety-one still stand. The other eighteen are not fallen; they are simply not there, and the ground where they stood is smooth.

lore.title: On the Breaking
lore.text: There was one light. It was not a god and made no demands; it lit things, and things that are lit grow. Then it broke. Nobody agrees on the hour, because every clock in the kingdom stopped at a different one.

lore.title: On Shards
lore.text: A shard is not a piece of the light. It is a piece of the light's intention, which is why it keeps working. A hand cut from an arm will not grip. A shard cut from the Spirit still shines, and still tries.

lore.title: On Hollowing
lore.text: The dead here do not rise. They were never permitted to finish lying down. A shard settles into whatever is nearest and works it like a glove, and the glove remembers being a hand, and that memory is the whole of the horror.

lore.title: On the Vesselborn
lore.text: Most people who take up a shard go out like a wick in a draught: bright, briefly, then a smell in the room. A few do not. Nobody can tell in advance which few. The kingdom tested for it the only way available.

lore.title: The Road Law
lore.text: Arm's length was the whole of the law. Anything closer than arm's length was a matter between you and it, and the crown declined to be involved.

lore.title: Notice of Relief
lore.text: TO THE WARDEN OF THE SOUTHERN ROAD: you are relieved of your post with thanks. Return by the first thaw. — Unsent. Found in a satchel in a drift, forty years of thaws later.

lore.title: The Tithe
lore.text: The fen takes what it takes. The Mirelord only made it regular. One in ten, counted aloud, and the other nine returned — changed, but returned, which was more than anywhere else could promise.

lore.title: Fen-Wife's Prayer
lore.text: Not my boy. Not this year. I will give you the goat, the good knife and the second-best name I know. Not my boy.

lore.title: On the Founding of Bells
lore.text: Seven were cast in one pour so that they would agree. Six agreed. The seventh came out of the mould with a flaw shaped like a word, and the founder wept, and hung it anyway.

lore.title: The Bell Rule
lore.text: Six for the dead, at any hour. The seventh only when there is somebody living to hear it. This was written as a comfort. It reads now as a countdown.

lore.title: At the First Hearth
lore.text: Every fire in the kingdom was lit from this one, and carried out, and carried on. When the carrying stopped, nobody thought to tell the man tending the first one. It would have been a strange thing to say.

lore.title: The Tenders' Argument
lore.text: Burn them and they do not walk. That was the argument. It was correct. It required, however, that somebody keep burning them, forever, and nobody had costed the forever.

lore.title: On the Empty Chair
lore.text: He held court standing for thirty-one years. Petitioners found it unnerving. He said a man who sits down in a room like this has agreed to something.

lore.title: The Abdication
lore.text: It was written, witnessed and sealed. It was never delivered, because there was no longer anyone with the standing to receive it, and a document like that read aloud to an empty hall becomes something else entirely.

lore.title: On the Long Winter
lore.text: The season was pinned in place so the rest could be put right. This was described at the time as a temporary measure. It has been temporary for a hundred and forty years.

lore.title: The Nine Cairns
lore.text: Nine parties went up to ask the Colossus to let go. Nine cairns. The tenth party did not go up, and built no cairn, and is generally considered to have handled it best.

lore.title: On the Rift
lore.text: It is not a door. A door implies somebody put it there. It is a hole, and things come through holes the way weather does — without invitation, without malice, and without any interest in the room.

lore.title: Sideways
lore.text: Everything that comes out of the Scar arrives at an angle to the world. You can hear it: their footsteps land slightly before they do.

lore.title: On the Orchard
lore.text: It was planted. That is the part people cannot get past. Somebody surveyed the ground, measured the rows, and planted them, and the rows are straight, and they are still straight.

lore.title: Between the Regions
lore.text: The land between named places has no name and no law and very few graves, because burying takes two people and out here there is rarely a second.

lore.title: On Beacons
lore.text: They were lit to be seen from the next one along. When enough of them went dark the chain broke into islands, and the islands forgot they had ever been a chain, and that is most of what happened to the kingdom.

lore.title: On Souls
lore.text: What you take off the dead is not their soul. It is the small amount of light they had left over after being themselves. Spend it. They cannot, and would not thank you for holding it.

lore.title: On Lesser Graces
lore.text: A shard too small to animate anything settles instead, and warms a few feet of ground, and will let you rest there. This is not mercy. It is a candle being a candle.

lore.title: The Smiths
lore.text: There is always a smith. Nobody has ever found where the next one comes from, and the smiths, when asked, look up briefly and go back to the work.

lore.title: The Hermits
lore.text: They stayed because leaving means choosing a direction, and choosing a direction means believing one of them is better. They have declined to believe that, and are, on the evidence, doing fine.

lore.title: On Taking a Weapon
lore.text: The dead do not object. A blade held by a husk was somebody's, once, and has been waiting through the whole intervening arrangement for a hand that would use it on purpose.

lore.title: The Survey of the Counted Ring
lore.text: Eighteen stones were raised on the level ground, and the Reach is level enough that a man can see all eighteen at once without turning his head. Seventeen stand. The eighteenth is not fallen and there is no hole where it stood; the grass there is simply older than the grass around it.

lore.title: Overheard on the Level Road
lore.text: Fifteen. Sixteen. Seventeen. — then a pause exactly one stone long, which is the part that gets into you, and then, without any change in his voice at all: one.

lore.title: The Last Dry Room
lore.text: The March agreed to go under. It was a vote, and it carried, and people packed accordingly. The forge did not vote. The water came up the steps, and around the walls, and stopped at the door, because the man inside had been told to let nothing out and had never been told the rule ran only one way.

lore.title: The Order to the Forge
lore.text: KEEP IT LIT UNTIL RELIEVED. Four words, and a clerk's initials, and no date. The clerk meant the fire. Every fire in the kingdom was lit from the Cinder Flats and carried out; his was the one they carried it to last, and nobody thought to write the sentence that ends it.

lore.title: On the Long Pit
lore.text: The orchard was planted in rows and the rows are straight. The pit is not a row. It is where the rows go when they fail, and it was dug wider each season by people who had stopped surveying and started only digging, and at some point the digging became the crop.

lore.title: The Pruner's Complaint
lore.text: Ground that is fed on a schedule learns the schedule. I said so at the third planting and I was told to mind the rows. I have minded the rows. The rows are fine. It is the pit that is putting out new growth, and none of it is fruit.

lore.title: The Three Ends
lore.text: Reforge it, and the light comes back with everything it lit still inside it. Scatter it, and the dark is honest at last. Take it, and there is a new light, and it is you, and it will also break. Choose. Everyone before you chose. That is why there is a choice left.

lore.title: The Fourth End
lore.text: Reforge it, scatter it, take it. The rite lists three because the rite was written by people who measured light in kingdoms. A lamp is not in the rite. A lamp is one room’s worth of yes. Nobody has ever tried it, because everyone who got this far had already agreed about what a light is for, and the agreement was the ninth step all along.

lore.title: The Blade Eleven Years Late
lore.text: Commissioned at the wayside forge by a man who went west and whom the road did not send back. Halvard Kenn hung it unfinished on the back rack and quoted for it every spring, out loud, to nobody. A blade on a wall is just an expensive apology; he has said so for eleven years, and left it on the wall for eleven years, and the two facts have never been introduced.

lore.title: Boneknapper
lore.text: Forged for the orchard, where the trees come up in the shape of bone and want pruning by somebody with a strong stomach. Nesh Barrow has carried it for eleven years and never once put it to a tree. He keeps it edged for the blightborn that plant things in his beds at night, in rows, tidily, which is the part he minds.

lore.title: Issued, Never Drawn
lore.text: Eleven sets of banded mitts, stamped for a relief column that was mustered, provisioned and never sent. The stamp is the only paperwork on the whole road that was completed on time. They turn up on the shoulders of strangers now, out of a chest at the crossroads that nobody admits to filling, and the buckles are still the issue pattern.

lore.title: The Banded Coat
lore.text: A roadwarden's coat outlives its warden by about four owners. The lining carries the post number, the hem carries the weather, and by the third wearer nobody can read either. Orrin Stave stood forty-one years in his and signed for the mail as O. Stove, because the lamp-wife wrote it wrong the first time and he never had the heart to correct a woman with that much else to do.

lore.title: Hearth Axe
lore.text: Wide, short-hafted, and made for splitting kindling rather than argument. Every fire in the kingdom was lit off the first hearth and carried outward, so the tenders kept axes and not swords, and Ondrey Sparr has an axe to this day. He has fed a fire nobody has come to collect from in two hundred years. He was told to keep it. Nobody has been sent to say the keeping is finished.

lore.title: Taken in Trade for a Bell
lore.text: A man came to the founder's yard wanting a bell and was told, correctly, that he could not have one: a bell is a promise, and Grieve Tull had stopped making those. The man left the sword anyway and did not come back for it. It has been on the bench under a cloth ever since, priced high enough that nobody buys it and honestly enough that nobody argues.

lore.title: Two Sets of Initials
lore.text: Short, thin, and ground down on one side from lifting offerings off graves without waking the neighbours. There are two sets of initials on the tang, one filed nearly out. Tabb the Shorter will tell you the price and not the story; the Taller is eight feet under a good stone that was paid for out of stock he would have sold cheaper.

lore.title: The Tenth Stone, Uncut
lore.text: Nine milestones on the kiln road say NINE LEAGUES TO FERROW and are correct about the distance and wrong about Ferrow. The tenth was set and never lettered. Peth Ivory kept the nine for nineteen years before anyone told her what the blank one was, and she has written the finding in the margin of the road law, where the road law has room for exactly one more line.

lore.title: A Lamp Kept Out
lore.text: A house lamp, small, brass, with a century-old wick and one good burn left in it. It was lit once, on the night the sky went out, by a woman who held it up so the road could find its way. Her daughter has kept it unlit ever since, in case the keeping was the point. It was not. The lighting was the point, and Maren Wick worked that out eleven years too late to be pleased about it.

lore.title: The Bow at the Top of the Stair
lore.text: Hollowwood, unstrung for eleven years at the head of the obsidian stair, kept by a woman who came out to the flats to find a man who went to tend the first fire and did not write. Yrsa Lound has counted four hundred steps down and never once counted them coming up. Down is a thing you are doing. Up is a thing being done to you.

lore.title: Nine Elms, Eleven Trees
lore.text: A beacon post on the mill track, lettered in stone a hundred and forty years ago by somebody who did not check. There are eleven elms at Nine Elms. Gilly Ash has been up twice to be sure and will not put a chisel to it, on the grounds that it is the only number in this country that anybody bothered to write down.

lore.title: Signed on the Inside
lore.text: Frostmarch anchor iron is signed where the ice gets at it and no buyer will ever look. Torv Nendel learned the habit in eleven weeks at a bellfounder's yard where he was not permitted to sign anything, and has done it to every chain, anchor and greatsword since. Halda Rime's tenth cairn is capped with a plate of it. She did not ask for the signature and has not scraped it off.

lore.title: A Door With No Handle
lore.text: Under the beacon stones there is a second floor nobody laid. The door is iron, sealed with a mark you have seen on every beacon and never noticed: an open hand, with one finger missing. It is warm. Something on the other side is waiting to be finished.

lore.title: Vaultwarden's Roll, Last Page
lore.text: Third seal checked. Lastlight still unfinished; the smith says the final verse must be earned, not cut. Verdict sleeps. The bow is restless. If the Spirit is ever put right, open the vaults. If it is not, open them anyway. Someone should know we tried.

lore.title: The Legend of the Ninth Step (Incomplete)
lore.text: Every telling of the rite stops at the eighth step. The ninth is scratched out in every copy, except one, which is not scratched out but simply missing, the page cut cleanly away. Who keeps a page they are ashamed of? Who keeps a page they are saving for later?

lore.title: Chalk Mark on a Merchant's Stall
lore.text: SOLD OUT. BACK WHEN THE DOORS OPEN. The handwriting matches no one in the kingdom. The stall was not here yesterday. The chalk is still wet, and the merchant's boots left no prints going away.

lore.title: A Fragment Not of This Steel
lore.text: A sliver of a single-edged blade, folded so many times the grain looks like water. The hamon line is a wave no smith here would draw. Wrapped around the tang is a paper slip in brushwork you cannot read, and one drawn symbol you can: a petal.

lore.title: A Petal in the Ash
lore.text: Pale pink, five lobes, perfectly preserved in the cinders where nothing has bloomed for a century. No tree here grows it. The wind that brought it came from the east, over the sea, from somewhere the light is apparently still on.

lore.title: Harbour Note, Grey Strand
lore.text: Ship seen on the horizon three nights running. Red sails, square, with a gate painted on them: two posts and two beams. Never closer, never further. Carrow says it is waiting for someone to light the strand beacon so it knows the kingdom is still here.

story.title: The Wick
story.text: You wake on the verge road with a splinter of something bright under the breastbone and no memory of agreeing to it. This is normal. Nobody has ever agreed to it. The rite requires a child, a promise, and a ninth step that everyone who has read it has scratched through — and you are what is left when the ninth step is performed anyway.

story.title: First Light
story.text: The beacon takes your shard's measure and lights, badly, for the first time in a century. It has been waiting to be told what it is by something that knew. Now it knows, and it can tell the next beacon along, and the next — if you can get there.

story.title: The Road That Ended
story.text: The Warden had a shard too, and it had made a very simple thing of him: keep the road. He kept it after the road stopped going anywhere, after the ash, after the relief order that was written and never sent. What came out of him when he fell was not a soul. It was an instruction, still running, and now it is yours to carry.

story.title: One in Ten
story.text: The Mirelord kept books. That was all the shard made of him: a talent for counting, applied without pause for two hundred years, until the counting was the whole person. You take his tally and understand something unpleasant — a shard does not possess you. It finds the one thing you already were, and turns it up until nothing else fits.

story.title: What the Shards Are
story.text: Two now, under the ribs, and they do not sit quietly together. Each remembers being part of one thing and each is trying, in its small stubborn way, to reassemble the rest of it inside you. You are not gathering trophies. You are being used as a table on which something is putting itself back together.

story.title: The Seventh, Unrung
story.text: The Choir sang six for the dead and held the seventh for the living. There have been no living here for a long time, and the note has been held so long that it has stopped being music and started being pressure. When it finally breaks over you, you understand that patience and madness are the same substance at different temperatures.

story.title: The Kept Flame
story.text: He was told to keep the first fire. Everything else in the kingdom was lit from it and carried outward, and when the carrying stopped no messenger came to say the fire was no longer needed, because saying so would have been absurd — a fire is always needed. He was correct. He was correct for two hundred years, and it cost everything, and he was still correct.

story.title: The Empty Chair
story.text: The King never sat, because sitting is agreement, and he would not agree to a kingdom in this condition. He wrote his abdication and could not deliver it: there was no one left with standing to receive a crown. So he stood, holding it, for thirty-one years, and the shard obliged him by making the standing permanent.

story.title: The Long Winter
story.text: The Colossus was set to hold the season still while the rest of it was put right. Nobody came back to say the rest of it had failed. It has been holding a page open for a book that stopped being written, and when it finally lets go the thaw takes eleven days and drowns four regions, and that, too, is on you.

story.title: Sideways
story.text: The Seraph is the first thing you kill that never held a shard at all. It came through the hole the Spirit left going out, the way weather comes through a broken window. It had no instruction, no grief, no two-hundred-year post to keep. It was simply here, at an angle, and that is somehow worse than all the rest of them.

story.title: Seven Shards, One Hand
story.text: You are very bright now, and people go quiet when you walk into a room, and you have begun keeping a road you have never seen, counting things in tens, standing rather than sitting. Seven instructions running at once in one body. The Vesselborn are not chosen for strength. They are chosen for having enough room.

story.title: The Hollow of Lights
story.text: You find the place it fell, at the far corner of everything, and it is not a crater. It is a hollow — a shape of absence exactly the size of the thing that used to be there, and still falling, very slowly, the way a note decays. Everything you have carried here begins to lean toward it.

story.title: What Is Left of the Light
story.text: It was never a god. It lit things, and things that are lit grow, and then it broke — without malice, without warning, taking the room with it. What you fight in the Hollow is not its ghost. It is the last unbroken piece, still trying to do the only thing it ever did, and it cannot understand why the world keeps flinching.

story.title: Ending: Reforge
story.text: You put the shards back. The light returns whole, and with it everything it ever lit — the Warden's road, the tally, the seventh note, the standing King. All of it, restored exactly as it was, including the flaw that broke it. Somewhere a child is being measured for a rite. The dawn is genuinely beautiful. It will hold for a while.

story.title: Ending: Scatter
story.text: You open your hands and let it go, all of it, in every direction, too fine ever to gather again. The husks lie down. The bells stop. The Warden's road is just a road, going nowhere, honestly. It is the first honest dark in two centuries, and nothing in it grows, and nothing in it is held against its will.

story.title: Ending: Take
story.text: You keep it. All seven, and the eighth, and the room you had for them turns out to have been the point. The light is yours now and it is not the same light, because it has opinions, and a face, and a memory of walking. You will be very good at this. You will be very good at this for a long time, and then, exactly like the last one, you will break — and someone will wake on a verge road with a splinter of you under the breastbone, and not remember agreeing.

story.title: Ending: Kindle
story.text: You do not reforge it, and you do not scatter it, and you do not keep it. You pour all of it — seven instructions, the last unbroken piece, a jar of stolen beacon-light and a century of careful dark — into a house lamp with one burn left in its wick. It takes. It lights a table, not a kingdom. Nothing grows by it except whatever chooses to sit down. Somewhere north, a woman feels her mother’s room get warmer, and does not ask.

story.title: Epilogue: The Unfinished Legend
story.text: The kingdom is quiet in whatever way you chose. But the beacons still have a second floor nobody laid, the sealed vaults have started to hum, and a merchant who was never here has chalked SOLD OUT on an empty stall. Far to the east, past the Grey Strand, a ship with red sails has finally turned toward land.

skills.name: Hollowwood Sweep
skills.description: The cut the road-wardens taught first, because it clears a path and asks nothing clever of you.

skills.name: Reaping Turn
skills.description: A harvester’s motion, kept exactly as it was and used for something else.

skills.name: Gravecutter
skills.description: Swung low, through the knees, the way you would clear headstones that had begun to lean.

skills.name: Low Lantern
skills.description: Held down and out like a lamp, so whatever comes at you meets the edge before it meets you.

skills.name: Widow’s Arc
skills.description: A long, unhurried cut named for a woman who only ever made one.

skills.name: Bell-Swing
skills.description: The full-body pull of a bell-rope, ending where a bell is not.

skills.name: The King’s Measure
skills.description: He measured every room he entered by whether this cut would fit in it. Most did not.

skills.name: Saltwind Cut
skills.description: Learned on a deck that would not hold still, which is why it never needs firm ground.

skills.name: Tithe of Edges
skills.description: One in ten of everything, the fen says, and it does not specify of what.

skills.name: The Long Vigil
skills.description: Stand, and lean, and put the point exactly where the road will be.

skills.name: Needle Through Cloth
skills.description: A tailor’s phrase for it. She did not think the comparison was funny either.

skills.name: Impaling March
skills.description: The formation advance of a province that agreed to go under. They kept marching anyway.

skills.name: The Quiet Answer
skills.description: For when a question has been asked at close range and cannot be talked out of.

skills.name: Lance of Ash
skills.description: The Reach is level for a hundred miles, so they built a strike that could cross it.

skills.name: Pinning Oath
skills.description: You swear it into the ground through whatever happens to be standing there.

skills.name: Hollow Point
skills.description: Aimed at where the person used to be, which on a husk is still the fastest way through.

skills.name: Three Debts
skills.description: Three strokes, and the road-wardens were careful to say they were owed, not taken.

skills.name: Reckoning of the Ledger
skills.description: The Mirefen keeps accounts in wounds because paper rots and wounds do not.

skills.name: Hammerfall Cadence
skills.description: Smiths count it out loud. It is the only work-song left that anybody finishes.

skills.name: Tally of Small Wounds
skills.description: None of them would have mattered. That was rather the arithmetic.

skills.name: Pilgrim’s Cadence
skills.description: Step, strike, step, strike. It is how they cross the Flats without thinking about it.

skills.name: Seven Bells
skills.description: Six halls sing. The seventh is struck, once for each thing it will not say.

skills.name: Shearing Pass
skills.description: Two edges, opposite directions, and no interval worth stepping into.

skills.name: Flurry of Small Mercies
skills.description: The blightborn call it mercy because it is quick. Nobody who received it agreed.

skills.name: The Turning
skills.description: One full revolution, committed to before you know what is behind you.

skills.name: Mourner’s Wheel
skills.description: They turned three times at the graveside. Someone realised it also worked.

skills.name: Gale of Edges
skills.description: Fast enough that the grey air keeps turning after you stop.

skills.name: Millstone
skills.description: Slow, total, and indifferent to what is fed into it.

skills.name: Lash Carousel
skills.description: The whip does the circle for you; you only have to keep your feet.

skills.name: Riftwhirl
skills.description: Everything sideways at once. The Scar teaches it by accident, to anyone who lingers.

skills.name: Knuckle Carousel
skills.description: Both fists out, heels planted, and a great deal of trust in your own elbows.

skills.name: The Toll
skills.description: Brought down flat, so the ground rings and the ringing is the second hit.

skills.name: Kneeling Stone
skills.description: A mason’s trick: don’t hit the thing, hit what the thing is standing on.

skills.name: Cinderquake
skills.description: Every fire in the kingdom was lit from here, and some of it is still under the crust.

skills.name: Collapse of the Seventh Hall
skills.description: It came down all at once and in tune, which the choir insists was intentional.

skills.name: Root-Shudder
skills.description: The Hollowwood is one tree, mostly, and it does notice being struck.

skills.name: Frostbreak
skills.description: The Frostmarch is pinned in place. Hit it hard enough and a little of it comes loose.

skills.name: Step Through the Grey
skills.description: You are on the other side of them before the grey has finished closing.

skills.name: Roadbreaker
skills.description: Shoulder first, weapon second, apology never.

skills.name: Drawn Step
skills.description: The blade is not out until it is already through. Mourners taught it; nobody taught them.

skills.name: Lamplight Rush
skills.description: Named for how the lantern streaks when you run with it, which is the last thing they see.

skills.name: Riftstep
skills.description: Sideways, briefly, through somewhere that does not want you and cannot stop you.

skills.name: Wading Charge
skills.description: The Sunken March learned to run in water. On dry ground it is frankly unfair.

skills.name: Hound’s Line
skills.description: Straight, low, and without the courtesy of a wind-up. The ashhounds do not wind up either.

skills.name: Ash-Fletched Volley
skills.description: Three shafts, cut from the Reach, loosed on one breath.

skills.name: Winch-and-Loose
skills.description: You do not aim a winch crossbow so much as decide, well in advance, where it will go.

skills.name: Siege Shaft
skills.description: Built for walls. Walls are rarer now than the things it is used on.

skills.name: Spirit Lance
skills.description: A shard, drawn long and thin, and asked politely to travel.

skills.name: Prayer of Embers
skills.description: Said quickly, in five parts, none of which are for the person you are saying it at.

skills.name: Struck Note
skills.description: One clean tone, travelling outward, passing through whatever is not paying attention.

skills.name: Parting Edge
skills.description: You throw it. You had better have decided about that beforehand.

skills.name: Grey Wave
skills.description: The cut keeps going after the blade has stopped. Nobody has explained this satisfactorily.

skills.name: Hailmark
skills.description: The Frostmarch pins the season in place; a good archer can loose a piece of it.

skills.name: Sporecast
skills.description: The fen sends its tithe on ahead, slowly, and it always arrives.

skills.name: Keep the Flame
skills.description: The tenders’ whole argument, in one gesture: it is not yours, but it is your turn.

skills.name: The Road Law
skills.description: Walk in the middle. Do not answer the trees. Whatever is behind you is behind you.

skills.name: Sharpening Vow
skills.description: Said over the edge, not to it. The edge is not the part that needs convincing.

skills.name: Quickened Grief
skills.description: It moves you along. That is the only kind anyone here has time for.

skills.name: Hymn of the Sixth Hall
skills.description: Six halls sing and one does not. The sixth is the one that keeps you standing.

skills.name: Winter Temper
skills.description: Cold the steel until it stops arguing. Then cold your hands until they stop too.

skills.name: Bloodwake
skills.description: You stop bandaging it. It stops being a problem and starts being a supply.

skills.name: Steady Hand
skills.description: The archers’ discipline: breathe out, and do not care yet.

skills.name: Hold the Light In
skills.description: A vessel is only a shape you agree to keep. Agree harder, for a while.

skills.name: Warden’s Answer
skills.description: Take the blow on the flat, and give the reply the road-law recommends.

skills.name: Turning Palm
skills.description: You do not stop it. You agree with it, briefly, and then disagree.

skills.name: Measured Stance
skills.description: Court duelling, kept intact by people who no longer have a court.

skills.name: Iron Vigil
skills.description: Root, and wait, and let the first mistake be theirs.

skills.name: Hollow Patience
skills.description: The husks have it in abundance. It is the only thing they kept.

skills.name: Catching Cord
skills.description: A whip can take a blade out of a hand. It rarely gives it back.

skills.name: Braced Stock
skills.description: Take it on the stock, then put the bolt where the swing came from.

skills.name: Fen-Thorn Fence
skills.description: The Mirefen grows its own borders. Ask it nicely and it will grow one here.

skills.name: Ring of Small Fires
skills.description: The tenders keep a great many small ones so that no large one is ever needed.

skills.name: Grave Lanterns
skills.description: Four lights, set down where they will do the most good, which is not near you.

skills.name: Bonemeal Scatter
skills.description: The Orchard was planted deliberately. So is this, and for the same reason.

skills.name: Nine Cairns
skills.description: They stacked nine and the winter stopped where the ninth was. Mostly.

skills.name: Bell Garden
skills.description: Six of them, planted in a curve, and all of them ringing the same held note.

skills.name: Ember Stakes
skills.description: Driven into the ash in a line, still hot, and left to do the arguing.

skills.name: Felling Stroke
skills.description: Woodcutters aim a hand’s width past the far side of the trunk. The habit transfers.

skills.name: Lit Wick
skills.description: A small flame, kept close, burning something you would rather not name.

skills.name: Upraised Seal
skills.description: Hold it up. Whatever is coming has to get past the argument first.

skills.name: Split the Light
skills.description: One bolt into the prism, three out of it, and only the middle one was aimed.

skills.name: Lattice
skills.description: Five bolts on five angles, hung in the air for as long as it takes you to regret standing there.

skills.name: The Long Line
skills.description: Drawn once, all the way to whatever is at the end of it, and everything in between is incidental.

skills.name: Hold It Open
skills.description: The staff will do this for as long as you can afford it, and it has no opinion about when that is.

skills.name: Stand the Lens
skills.description: A moment spent aligning it, paid back over the minute after.

skills.name: Grounding Discharge
skills.description: Everything the shaft has been holding, put into the floor at once, because the floor cannot dodge.

skills.name: Needle of Light
skills.description: Short, precise and over before the sound arrives, which several people have found upsetting.

skills.name: Refraction
skills.description: Not a block. The blow arrives and the lens decides it arrived somewhere else.

skills.name: Lightstep
skills.description: You are not fast. The rod is fast, and it has hold of your wrist.

skills.name: Set a Node
skills.description: Left standing where you put it, humming, until something walks close enough to complete the circuit.

npcs.name: Ilex Vore
npcs.title: Who Went Through and Came Back

npcs.name: Otherworldly Merchant
npcs.title: Trading Out of the Rift Scar

lines: You are the fourth this year. The other three went that way, and one of them came back as far as the gate.
Do not tell me your name. I have found it easier since I stopped learning them.

choices.text: You keep a lamp you have not lit.

lines: It was a chain once. Each one told the next what it had seen, and the last one told the capital, and the capital did something about it.
The last hundred years it has been telling nobody. I keep the wick trimmed anyway. That is the whole of my occupation.
Because a beacon takes the measure of whoever lights it, and reports it onward. I would not care to be reported.
You have something in you it will recognise. That is not a compliment. It is only a fact about you, the way a wet coat is a fact.
A splinter. There were a great many, once, all of one thing, and it came apart over this kingdom the way a lamp comes apart on a floor.

The pieces went into whoever was standing nearest. Wardens, kings, a woman who kept books. It does not make you into something. It finds the one thing you already were and turns it up until nothing else fits.

choices.text: Then it can be taken out.

lines: How would I know. Go far enough and you will find out, which is the cruel part of the arrangement.
Some of them were quite pleasant people beforehand.
Three ways, they say, and I have never met anyone who got as far as choosing between them.
There is a man at the far gate who did. Ask him, if you live that long, and mind that he is not pleasant company about it.
It is four steps behind me. I have kept the wick dry for a century, so if it does not take, the fault is yours.
A house lamp. Small. My mother's, and it has never been lit in my keeping, which I used to think was thrift.
Wornstone, five, ground fine, and a beacon lit at the Leaning Gate so I know the chain still carries. Then I will light it and see what I have been saving.
Five. Not four with an apology.
Yes. That is the sensible answer and I have been giving it to myself for eleven years.
Five pieces of wornstone and a light at the Leaning Gate. I have not moved the requirements since you left.

choices.text: What is the lamp really for?

lines: My mother lit it the night the sky went out, to see by. It has been out since and I have not wanted to know whether that was the lamp or the world.
You may find that a small thing to be frightened of. You have not sat with it eleven years.
The Gate is lit. I saw it off the water an hour before you came, and I sat down, which I do not do.
Give me the stone.
It takes. It is a very ordinary flame and the room is exactly as I left it, which is what I was afraid of, and it turns out that is bearable.
Take this. You will be somewhere worse than here soon enough.
It carried. Two hours after you lit it the Leaning Gate answered, faintly, and something further out answered that.
I have not heard the chain speak since I was a girl. I am not certain it is good news. It is only news.
West along the verge, where the road stops pretending. There is a Warden on it who was told to keep it and was never told to stop.
He will not listen. Wardens do not. That is what makes them wardens and it is also what has to be done about him.
You are brighter. Do not thank me for noticing; it is not a thing I would want said about me.
The road is quiet now, and I find I liked it better when someone was keeping it badly than not at all.
No. And now the part of him that would not stop is in you, and you will find yourself checking the verge for washouts and not knowing why.
Count them, when you take them. It helps to know how much of what you are doing is yours.
Stand further off. No — that was rude and I meant it, so I will not take it back.
You go quiet when you walk in. Seven of them talking at once inside one person, and none of them saying anything they were not told to say two hundred years ago.

choices.text: You were right about the counting.

lines: That is what the Warden said, near the end, to a relief officer who was not there.
Go on to the corner of everything. If you come back, come back at a distance, and do not light anything on your way in.
Then you are further along than the other three. One of them stopped counting at four and I watched the rest of it happen from the doorway.
It is not a rescue, keeping count. It only means the last thought is yours.
The chain has gone quiet again, all at once, the way it did when I was nine.
I do not know what you did and I am not going to ask. I have trimmed the wick. It is enough occupation for one life.
The wick is dry, the oil is old, and the road goes west whether anyone uses it or not.

A man came up the verge last week, first traveller in a month. He said there is a person at the far corner keeping light in a jar, and a dead woman who remembers my mother, and that you have spoken with both.
My mother lit this lamp the night the sky went out, and held it up, and the road found its way by it. I have been keeping it out ever since in case the keeping was the point.
It was not. The lighting was the point. Take it to the far corner, and when they offer you the three ways, ask whether a fourth would fit in something this small.
Mind the wick. It is a century old and it has one good burn in it, and so, between us, do you.
Do not light it on the way. It is not for the road. It is for after the road.
You still have it. Good. I can feel the house being lighter by exactly one lamp, and it is not an unpleasant feeling, and I want it to stay gone.
The chain is dark again. But there is one light at the far corner of everything, very small, and it is not asking to be believed in. It is only lit.
That is my mother’s lamp. I would know it across a kingdom. Go and sit somewhere, Vesselborn. The rest of this is the lamp’s to do, at the lamp’s pace, and it has never once hurried.
So you have met the man at the far gate.
He will have counted you before you were through the arch. They all do, the ones who stop.

I knew him when the road still had carts on it. He was not a careful man then. Six shards and a hundred years have made him careful, and careful is what he calls it, and I would call it something else if he were not right.

choices.text: He says the seventh makes them agree.

lines: Then he told you the true part first, which is more than he managed for the girl of nineteen.
Do not let him do your arithmetic. He is very good at it, and he has had a century to make it come out the way it came out.
Everyone this side of the ash knew him. He came up the verge twice a year with the mail, and once with a broken arm, and he sat where you are standing and complained about the hill.
I do not tell him I remember. He has arranged his hundred years so that nothing before them counts, and I am not going to be the draught under that door.
The bells have stopped. I heard it here four days late, the way you hear a thing that has stopped rather than started.

There is a woman in that building with her hand on a wall — Vantine Aske, if she still answers to it. If she is standing, tell her a lamp-wife on the verge says the wick is dry and the chain still carries.
It is not worth much. It was sent, which is the whole of it.
You came up the verge in a dead person's coat and did not know it, which is the kindest way to wear one.
There is a hand that keeps a chest at the crossroads. I have never learned whose the chest was, and I have made a policy of the not-learning.
Halvard Kenn will re-hang the buckles if you ask. He pretends not to notice whose coat it was. He notices.
You came back. I did not think the road brought anyone back.
There is a door under my beacon. It has been there longer than I have, and it has started to hum.
I will not open it. Somebody should, and I think you are getting tired of me saying that about everything.
Halt is the word, but I have stopped using it. Nobody halts and then I am obliged to do something about it.
This is the Warden's Post. I hold it. I have held it since the ash and I would like it recorded that I have never once left the boards.

choices.text: Nothing to say to a post.

lines: By the ledger, when the ledger comes back. It went down the road with a boy who was to have it stamped and returned within the month.
That was forty-one years ago. He was not a fast boy but he was not that slow.
Very likely. That does not relieve me. The order relieves me. A dead boy is a delay, not a discharge.
You may think that is a small distinction. It is the only one I have left.
There is a written relief. There must be. Nobody keeps a road for forty years without somebody, somewhere, writing down that it is over.
Find it. The ledger, with the countersign of the Warden on the west stretch. Then I will step off the boards and you may do what you like with the post.
Then it was desertion, and everything since was desertion, and the forty years were a man standing in the road for nothing.
You will forgive me for preferring the paperwork.
The ledger is a grey book with a strap. West, in the ruin they had the post office in, or wherever the road put it since.
And the countersign is on the Warden himself. He will not lend it.
Still the boards. The rain comes across from the mill about now.
Grain in, ore out, and the King's people on horses twice a year being unpleasant about the state of the culverts.
It went to a town called Ferrow. There is no Ferrow. I have had that confirmed by three separate people and I still keep the road to it.
That is the strap. Do not open it here, I will want to read it and I am not ready to read it.
The countersign. Has he given it.

choices.text: Not yet. He is still on the road.
He will not give it living.

lines: Then it is a book and not an order, and I am still on the boards. Go west.
No. He would not. He was a better warden than me, which I have had forty years to be honest about.
Do it properly. Do not make a mess of a man who was only obeying an instruction with nobody left to cancel it.
Read it to me. No — I will read it. My eyes are the only part of me the post has not used up.
Notice of relief, dated the eleventh, unstamped, undelivered, and countersigned in a hand I would know on a wall in the dark.
It is dated correctly. Lateness is the courier's business, not the order's.
I have had a long time to work out which of those to be angry at, and I have chosen the courier, who is dead. It is tidier.
There. Off the boards. It is three inches down and my knees have opinions about it.
Take the token. It was issued to me for the keeping of a road and I am no longer keeping anything. It still knows the way, which is more than I do now.
I sit now. I had forgotten it was allowed.
The road still goes west. I find I do not care where, and that is the strangest part of being finished.
Forty-one years for a piece of paper. Yes. And I would do it again, because the alternative was that the forty-one years had been nothing at all, and a man cannot carry that and a road.
The post is held. Move along or do not; I have stopped enforcing it.
You have walked further than I ever did. Then you have met her — the keeper at milestone nine, out on the Reach. Ivory. Still at her stone.

The southern road had two ends, and the law ran the whole length of it: arm’s length, and no further, and the crown declines the rest. I held this end. She holds that one. Neither of us ever knew the other was still standing.

Take her my warden’s token — the words will do; the token is the words. Tell her: the southern end is relieved, in order, with the paperwork read aloud. Tell her the road was held at both ends the whole time. A keeper should know she was never holding it alone.
She took it, then. Good. A road is a line between two people who agree it is a road; everything else is just ground.
Forty years I thought I was the last of the law. It turns out I was half of it. That is a much better thing to have been.
The Ashen Warden is off the road. I felt it in the boards under me, which is not possible, and which happened.
He had my post at the northern end. Same order, same paper, same relief that never came.
The difference between us is a grey book with a strap on it, and forty-one years of luck I did not earn.

choices.text: You are relieved. He was not.

lines: No. And I have had a week of sitting down, and spent most of it standing up out of habit and then remembering.
Do not say the shard kept him. The order kept him. The shard only made the keeping tidy.
The lamp-wife. Maren Wick. She signed for the mail at the verge and never once got my name right on the slip, and I never once corrected her.
Forty-one years of O. Stove.
If you are going back that way you may tell her I minded, and that I should like it left as Stove now. It is the only part of the record with any humour in it.
Tabb. The Shorter. There was a Taller and he is not here, and I would rather not go into the arithmetic of that.
You have the look of somebody who is going to be carrying a great deal soon and will want to put some of it down for coin.
Laid out honest. The prices are not honest but the goods are, and in this country that is the better half.
Whatever the Hollowwood has stopped needing. That is a broader category every year and I am not proud of how comfortable it has made me.
Grave offerings mostly. People leave good iron on the dead and the dead do not follow up.
From whom. Give me a name and an address and I will post it back.
No. Thought not. It is only theft while somebody is still expecting it.
Three offerings and the brigands off the mill track. They have been undercutting me, which takes some doing at my prices.
You get coin and a flask charge and my continued good opinion, which is worth less than the other two.
Three. And they must be off graves, not off the shelf at the mill, because I will know.
Fair. Everybody says no the first week.
One worth the telling. There is a light out past the far corner, and it goes out about an hour after anybody lights it.
Somebody is taking it. In a jar, is the version I was told, by a man who was drunk but specific.
His word, not mine. I sell jars, so I did not press him on the point.
Three offerings and the track cleared. I have not raised the number while you were out, which I could have.

choices.text: There is a girl at the mill who counts trees.

lines: Gilly. Yes. She has a cache under the fourth big rootwood and she thinks nobody has watched her walk to it.
Tell me where and the debt is settled today, in coin, and neither of us mentions it again.
There. Done, paid, and forgotten by me within the hour.
She will work it out. She counts things; that is rather the difficulty with her.
No. Well. I did not think you would, and I asked anyway, which tells you what I am.
Three, off graves, and the track quiet. You have done a week of my work in an afternoon and I resent it slightly.
Coin, and the charge, as agreed.
Settled. I will still overcharge you; that is business and not personal.
Come back when you have something heavy you have stopped loving.
Crossroads. Four ways, three of them bad, and I am on the fourth selling to people going down the other three.
You went and looked at a tree. People do not usually go and look at the tree. The tree relies on that.

All right. It is not a tree, it is a marker, and under it is everything I have lifted off the old graves this year, and Gilly has been counting her way toward it since the spring, and you have the face of somebody about to make that my problem.

choices.text: Put it back. All of it, every grave.

effects.text: Tabb will dig the rest back in. The count will come right.

choices.text: A third of it buys my silence.

lines: Fine. Fine. Take these — they were going back anyway, they were, I had a schedule.
You will want to be there when she recounts. She does the whole four hundred and six out loud and there is no talking during.
A third. You have salvager’s arithmetic in you somewhere, friend, and I mean that as flattery and warning both.
The tree stays a tree. Gilly keeps her miscount. Everybody sleeps, some of us less well.
You have been trading out of the scar. Do not look surprised. You have the walk of a man who has just been priced.
I sell jars, wornstone and other people's grave-iron at four times what it is worth, and I sleep.
That thing sells one of each of everything there will ever be. It is not a shop. It is a building, standing up, doing an impression of somebody who wants your money.
So is a toll bridge.
Every day and twice on the feast, if I had the coin and a way out afterwards.
That is not a defence of my character. That is the character.
Now the crossroads is lit I have to look at my own sign. It says TABB. Under it, in a different hand, THE SHORTER.
He was my brother. Four inches taller, and eight feet lower.
Between us we make the average man. That is his joke. I have kept making it, which is the arrangement.
Eight, and a good stone on top, bought out of stock he would have sold cheaper.
He would have called that theft. I call it interest.
Kept, thank you, and not spent on me.
Spend them on somebody who will need them this week. I have a stall, a roof, and a brother who has stopped growing.
Four hundred and six. That is the trees, not a greeting, and I have to say it out loud when somebody arrives or I lose my place.
Four hundred and six, last spring. It is three hundred and ninety now and I am not the one taking them.
Because everything else here has stopped having a number. The dead have no number. The years have no number since the ash.
The trees have a number. I check it. Then I know the day happened.
It is not, but you are the first to say so and I am going to keep it.
Hounds. They come down the mill track at dusk and go at the young wood, and I do not know what a hound wants with young wood but the count says they get it.
Six of them, roughly. I cannot be exact about hounds; they do not hold still to be counted.
Six. Then come back and I will show you the tree I do not count, which is the actual business.
There is nothing safer. That is why I chose trees; they are the safest thing left and they are being eaten.
Three hundred and eighty-eight. It was three hundred and ninety when you left, so you will understand my tone.

choices.text: What is the tree you do not count?

lines: When the hounds are down. Not before. If I say it first you will go and look and then I will have to know what you saw.
Six. Good. The count will hold now, and it is a nasty thing to be pleased about.
South of the mill, off the track, there is a rootwood with a man's coat still on it, and it has been growing round the coat. I have never gone close. You are the sort that goes close.

choices.text: Do not send me to look at that.

lines: No. Of course not. Nobody does.
Then it stays four hundred and six with one I do not count, and that is the arrangement, and it has held eleven years.
It is my father's coat. I know because I sewed the elbow badly and the badness is still there, going round the trunk.
Thank you. That is the whole of what I wanted and I could not go and get it. Take his axe. He would want it used on the hounds.
Four hundred and six. I have started counting him again.
Do not tell the salvager at the crossroads about the coat. He is not a bad man. He is only a man who would sell it.
The coat is gone off the rootwood and the elbow with it, and there are two sets of boot marks and one of them is yours.
Four hundred and six. Go away. Four hundred and six.
Three hundred and eighty-eight, and the light going, and you standing in my line of sight.
Four hundred and six. I counted twice and it held both times, and the ground by the mill track has been turned and patted down like a bed.
You did that. Do not tell me how; the how has a person in it, and I find I do not want a person in it. I want a number that holds, and I have one.
There is a beacon down the track called Nine Elms.
There are eleven elms at Nine Elms.
I have been up twice. Eleven. Somebody lettered that post a hundred and forty years ago, in stone, and got it wrong, and has been wrong at every traveller since, and is dead, and cannot be told.
Yes. That is the answer. I have had it available to me for eleven years and I go back and count anyway.
Four hundred and six. Eleven at the elms. The day happened.
I am not putting a chisel to the only number in this country somebody bothered to write down.
Do not put it on the anvil. Everybody puts it on the anvil and then I have to be polite about a broken thing at close range.
Halvard Kenn. I work kept iron. I do not work new iron and if that is what you have brought we can be brief.
Everything on the rack has been in something's hand and come out again. That is the only guarantee I offer and it is a real one.
Iron off a thing that was used until it broke. A hinge that swung forty years. A blade that was carried and not displayed.
New iron has not agreed to anything yet. Put a shard-touched edge on it and it takes the shape of whatever is nearest and holds it forever. Kept iron argues. I prefer a metal that argues.
Very likely. I have been wrong for thirty years in a way that has kept me alive and every man I know who was right is out on the verge holding a post.
Judge the method by the survivors.
Four pieces. And heat, which is the harder half — the wayside forge has been cold since the ash and it will not take from a match.
There is a beacon at the Warden's Post. Light it and this forge remembers what it is for. Do not ask me why. Ask the chain.
Then there is a longsword on the back rack that has been waiting eleven years for a reason, and you have just become one.
Then buy something or stand out of the light.
Four pieces of kept iron, and the Warden's Post lit. The order does not matter. The arrival does.

choices.text: What is on the back rack?

lines: A vigilkeeper's longsword, unfinished, because the man who commissioned it went west and the road did not send him back.
I have not sold it. I have also not finished it. You may draw your own conclusions about which of those is the sentiment.
The post is lit. I felt the forge take about the same hour, which I will not try to explain to you or to myself.
Give me the iron and stand back. This part is loud.
There. Finished, eleven years late, for the wrong hand. He would not have minded; he was not a sentimental man and neither is the sword.
Use it until it breaks. Then bring it back and it will be kept iron, and we start again.
Still swinging it, I see. Good. A blade on a wall is just an expensive apology.
The rack is open. Prices unchanged; I am not a merchant, I am a man with a rack.
Cold forge, warm opinions. Rack is there.
You have been up the reach to Cald Ferrin's forge. Do not tell me whether it was lit. I have a rule about asking.
He and I were apprenticed the same year to different men. I have kept a cold forge two hundred years out of superstition and he has kept one out of grief.
Mine is the cheaper reason and I know it.
Then this morning he is two hundred years braver than me, and I will hear nothing said against him. Including by him.
Bring me a blade this week and I will re-hang it for nothing. Do not ask again next week.
So do I. The difference is that he was standing under it with a boy's hand in his.
I was three regions south, being right about the weather.
Somebody has kitted you out of a chest. I know those buckles. There were eleven sets and they were issued, not sold.
Issued to a relief column that never went out. Whoever hands them round at the crossroads did not buy them either, and I have decided that is between him and the column.
Put it down. Not the sword — the hand.
You are holding my anvil-edge the way the Warden held his road, and the anvil has noticed.
Two hundred years of shoeing and edging and I have never been afraid of a customer. Come back when you have decided what you are. The rack will keep.
Mind the boards. Half of them are ship and half of them are what the ship was carrying, and I can no longer tell which by looking.
Ismay Coldkeel. I wreck. There is nothing here that is going anywhere, so I do not consider it a crime against navigation.
Everything that floated. That is not poetry, it is the tide chart. The Grey Strand is where the current gives up.
Grain barges, a chapel roof, a great many boots without feet in them, and then, later, a great many feet.
I am forty-one and I have opened nine hundred crates and every one of them was somebody's plan.
You get tired of plans. Not of the crates.
They came in with the tide and did not go out with it. Eight, near enough, in the keel where I have my winch.
I can work around a great deal. I cannot work around eight.
It took me two summers to set. I will die at that winch before I move it, which I appreciate is exactly the problem with everyone in this country.
Eight. And light the keel when you are done, because I do not go into that hull in the dark and I will not pretend otherwise.
Still eight. Or fewer. You would know better than me; I have not been in to check.
A strongbox I have wanted for two summers, and the crew that was carrying it when they stopped.
I have decided the strongbox is what I want. It is easier to hold one idea at a time down there.
Lit, and quiet. I went in with the winch and got the box and it was full of ledgers.
Two summers for ledgers. I laughed until I sat down in the water, which is the most honest hour I have had this year.
No. It was for two summers of having something to do that ended.
Take the falchion off the rack. It came off a strand-picker who did not have two summers.
Tithes. Ten columns, nine filled, the tenth blank down every page for two hundred pages.
Somebody in the fen has been keeping very good books. Take the falchion and go and see about it, and do not tell me what you find.
Keel is clear and the winch has not moved an inch. Both facts please me.
If you find anything heavy out there and cannot carry it, remember who owns the only working winch on this coast.
Boards, brine, and a hull that has stopped being a hull. Mind your footing.
The tide-reader sent a warning up the strand with legs on it. That is new. Say it exactly; he will have made you promise to.
Coming back for what was taken. Over the winch first.

You paid me my share out of the keel when you did not have to, so I will treat your mouth as honest even when it is his words in it. The winch goes up the strand this week. I have robbed the sea thirty years by knowing exactly when to be a coward.

effects.text: Ismay is moving her winch to higher ground.

lines: The tide-reader sends me a prophecy by courier. He has read water at me for years and the water has never once done what he said on the day he said it.
